Project report · city-digital-twin · Newcastle (NSW)

Twelve targets, five knobs, and no loop between them

A reading of one commit: every tracked area of the code, the simulator's own timing, the whole history from day 0, the documents and the controls, this project's place among 48 comparable city models, and 79 factors a decision simulator must contain — assembled to answer one question the session set: can this architecture reach equilibrium across twelve simultaneous mode targets, and would machine learning or a different architecture get it there?

Date 8 September 2026 HEAD 6cf0ffd Branch main Tree clean Session gate 17 of 18 pass — issues gated FAIL

The verdict

The instrument is good and getting better. The method for pointing it at its goal does not exist. This project has spent 29 days, 476 commits, 162 runs and 383.2 machine hours moving a scoreboard that reads 1 of 12 modes inside 10% — the same 0-or-1 it has oscillated between for eleven families — and the reason is not effort, patience or physics. It is that the only automated calibration path in the repository can move five registry fields of 482, two of them taxi-only; its objective contains four independent numbers against the goal's twelve modes; and the path is fatally broken at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:486-491, so it has never executed a single candidate. The tool itself says so, verbatim: "refusing to fit 5 parameters to 4 independent numbers: that is not a calibration."

Nothing here is a result. Only a run whose _run.json says ran_to_last_iteration is one, and the deepest citable reached_iteration across all 162 runs is 100, against a goal of 250. The two deepest runs the project ever executed — 67.4 h and 67.3 h on 21 August — carry no completion at all, because the record contract postdates them.

The session's directive

The central question: can this architecture converge?

Twelve mode targets, one simulator, and — measured at HEAD — no search between them. What follows is the diagnosis; the full method survey and the phased proposal are further down.

Read from aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct at iteration 100 (family F31, 25% sample, trips table). Ten of twelve modes are scored on deviation; truck is level-only and freight rail representational. Bars are clipped at ±260% — heavy rail's +247.2% is drawn, taxi's +178.4% and bike's +147.4% are inside the frame. Not a result: the run stopped at its gate.

What the tool says about itself

Running the calibrator's own plan mode at HEAD is the shortest route to the diagnosis. It prints, verbatim:

The objective contains 4 independent numbers.

A search over all of them would fit 5 parameters to 4 numbers.
Name at most 4 with --only. The movable set is:
   A.gradient.grade_clamp_pct                             20  sweep 10 - 35  [percent]
   A.parking.max_stay_min                                120  sweep 60 - 180  [minutes]
   C.scoring.activity_minimal_duration_s                 900  sweep 300 - 1800  [seconds]
   C.taxi.asc                                              0  sweep -2 - 0  [utility]
   C.taxi.wait_min                                         5  sweep 2 - 12  [minutes]

refusing to fit 5 parameters to 4 independent numbers: that is not a calibration.

Five fields of 482. Two of them are taxi-only. The single mode constant in the set — C.taxi.asc — belongs to the one mode that has no independent target, because fit.py:123-130 folds bike and taxi into one category. And one of the five, A.gradient.grade_clamp_pct, does not reach the model at run time at all: its consumer patches the shipped network at assembly time, so a candidate that moved it would be recorded in the run's provenance and change nothing.

Not one of the five can reach ride (−38.0%), heavy rail (+247.2%), light rail (−47.2%), bus (+54.6%), bike (+147.4%), ferry (−65.6%) or walk (−11.1%) — every mode that is failing.

And the path has never run

The loop hands registry keys to run_matsim.py's raw MATSim --set path (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:486-491); build_config:433-436 splits the dotted key on its first dot and set_mode_param raises. So --execute cannot complete one candidate. The correct pattern exists 40 lines away in src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py:89. This was reported in the previous pass and is still open.

cities/newcastle/params/C5_calibration.json records the position honestly: "free_parameters": [], "history": [], "calibrated": {}, "search_declined", and "constraints": {"feasible": false}. It was generated 2026-08-24 — fifteen days and twenty-five comparability families ago.

Identifiability is not the blocker

This is the finding that changes what to do about it. Counting properly: the goal needs 10 independent targets and there are ten mode constants to carry them (eleven choice modes, car as reference). That is a square, well-posed inversion — Berry (1994) gives it in closed form. The problem is not that the system is under-determined.

The problem is that of those ten constants, six are frozen by a recorded decision (DECISIONS.md §8.5, which names ASC absorption "the primary threat to validity"), two do not exist — motorbike is hard-coded 0.0 and ferry has no constant at all, inheriting asc_bus (C_behaviour.json:789) — and one is free and pointed at the mode with no target. The inversion is well-posed and the instrument has been deliberately disconnected from it.

Three things any optimiser would run into first

  1. The objective measures a different thing from the goal. CAL.objective.components is {"mode_share.mean_abs_pp": 1.0} — a mean over five folded HTS categories in percentage points. The goal is a maximum over twelve unfolded modes in relative per cent. Heavy rail and light rail sit inside one folded "public transport" cell with opposite signs, so the existing calibrator could improve its objective while making both worse. A folded car+motorbike error near zero hides motorbike at +13.7%.
  2. Innovation never switches off. EscortCoherenceListener.java:111-116 is a ReplanningListener that adds and selects plans every iteration with no innovation cutoff — so plans are still being created through the innovation-off tail that summarise_run.relaxation uses to declare a run "relaxed", on the stated basis that none are. Every relaxation verdict this project has recorded rests on that.
  3. Ride is supply-constrained, not utility-elastic. GatedSubtourModeChoice "refuses ride on a trip nobody drives". The binders already declare 108,629 bound trips — 19.4% of resident trips against a 20.6% target — and F31 measured ride's geometry at 9.17 km against 9.76 observed. The gap is roughly 20,151 short lifts (median 1.08 km) being walked instead. No constant creates a trip that plan generation did not create.

The tension that has to be named, not smuggled past

This has to be said plainly rather than smuggled past. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and GOAL.md step 3 say: 'Find the cause - missing data, a bias, an over-manipulated parameter - and fix it from the root. No workarounds, no COMPENSATING CONSTANTS.' DECISIONS 8.5 makes the same point sharper, freezing every mode constant with the rule that 'Proposal 9 names ASC absorption as the PRIMARY threat to validity: calibrating mode constants to observed patronage fits away the effect under test'. An ASC fixed-point loop is, definitionally, the systematic fitting of mode constants to observed shares. It IS the compensating-constant move, industrialised. The project cannot adopt it and simultaneously claim it has not. But the ban and the method are not equally right about every mode, and the distinction is diagnosable rather than rhetorical. A constant is LEGITIMATE where it stands in for genuinely unmodelled tastes that are constant across the choice situation — the residual 'everything else about liking buses' — which is what an ASC means in any estimated logit; every eqasim, ActivitySim and Open Berlin model in this survey carries one, and boptx exists to fit them. A constant is a COMPENSATING FIX where it absorbs a specific, nameable, ABSENT MECHANISM. This model has at least two of the latter, and they are measurable today. Heavy rail is +247.2% and there is NO CROWDING DISUTILITY IN SCORING AT ALL: `C.crowding.seated_multiplier` and `C.crowding.standing_multiplier` are declared, carry literature sweeps, have NO consumers, and their own descriptions say 'NOT carried into MATSim scoring (DECISIONS.md 9.3)', CORRECTION, verified after this report was first written: the transit fleet DOES carry standing room - bus 44 seated / 18 standing, ferry 149/51, rail 98/48, patched from published figures - so capacity binds physically and a full vehicle refuses boarding. What is absent is the DISUTILITY: MATSim core scores no crowding term at all, so a passenger stands at no cost. Driving `C.asc.rail` down until boardings match would be pricing a crowding penalty into a taste constant — a constant that would then be carried, wrong, into every scenario where rail capacity changes, which is the exact failure mode 8.5 was written to prevent. Ride is -38.0% and the cause is not utility either: `GatedSubtourModeChoice` 'refuses `ride` on a trip nobody drives', the four binder passes create 108,629 bound trips which would be 19.4% of resident trips against a 20.6% target, and the F31 gate shows ride's mean modelled trip at 9.17 km against an observed 9.76 (-6%) — so the SUPPLY is right and the PLACEMENT is right and the shortfall is that 20,151 short lifts (median 1.08 km) get walked instead of ridden. No value of `C.asc.car_passenger` creates a ride trip that plan generation did not create. Third, walk's modelled mean trip is 4.51 km against an observed 0.70, and 33.4% of PT routing requests find no transit route at all with 40.6% of the rest taking the network walk — a routing defect, not a taste. THE HONEST RESOLUTION, and it is a rule the project can actually enforce: an ASC may move ONLY for a mode whose deviation survives after every nameable mechanism is present, and the loop must REFUSE to move a constant for a mode carrying an open structural defect. Concretely: freeze `C.asc.rail` until crowding is in scoring or the target basis is corrected; freeze `C.asc.car_passenger` until ride's placement is fixed; freeze `C.asc.walk` until the PT routing failure is understood. Let the fixed point move bus, light rail, bike, motorbike and the two constants that do not yet exist (ferry, motorbike). That is not a compromise of the rule — it is the rule, applied per mode, with the evidence for each. And it is worth recording that agency practice has independently reached the same discipline from the other end: WFRC deliberately accepts base-year deviations of -6.6% to -12.1% on its low-ridership modes because 'calibrating to increase base year accuracy resulted in too large alternative specific constants (i.e. over calibrating these modes)' — an agency, in production, choosing a worse base-year fit over a constant it did not believe. That is precisely the judgement DECISIONS 8.5 is making, made by people who calibrate constants for a living.

The reference library is the reason this was affordable. Every stored row was one day old and inside its horizon, so not one stored fact was re-searched; the search budget went to gaps alone. A row carried forward is marked reused with its verification date.

The rating rubric

Each code area is rated 1–5 on five dimensions — correctness, clarity, testability, efficiency, constraints — and every cell carries its two strongest pieces of evidence. Ratings are never averaged across areas: a 2 in one area and a 4 in another are statements about different things.

What this report did not do

It launched no run, recompiled nothing, opened no issue, and edited no model, data or living document. It wrote three files: this report, its index row, and the refreshed reference library.

The convergence verdict

The number of modes inside 10% is not trending up; it is oscillating between 0 and 1 with no run of two, and it has never been measured at a depth the model's own record calls converged. The valid twelve-mode series across the eight families that produced one - F21 0, F22 1, F23 0, F24 1, F25 0, F26 0, F28 1, F31 1 - moves by exactly one mode either way, and the mode that is inside changes each time (bus at F22, motorbike at F24, car at F28 and F31), so even the single hit is not the same hit persisting. Two earlier readings that looked like progress (F12 and F13's heavy rail at -0.7% and -1.5%) were retracted by §9.100 as artefacts of a contaminated yardstick, which is the cleanest evidence in the record that the instrument moved as much as the model did. The record gives three reasons, all of them measured rather than argued. First, comparability: 31 family boundaries in 24 days, eight of them on one day, so no two consecutive readings may be differenced - PR #161 refuses that sentence explicitly - and the project has never accumulated two comparable observations of the same change. Second, depth: every arm since 21 August has stopped at or before iteration 100 under the GOAL loop's own stop rule, while the loop's target horizon is 250, so what the board reads is a transient, and §9.108 measured car, walk and pt still arriving between iterations 200 and 350. Third, the deficit is structural rather than parametric: ride has sat between -38% and -43% through eleven consecutive families of repairs, F25 falsified the demand-side explanation for it by raising the seeded share 31% with no movement in the realised share, and F31 then showed that the lifts the binder places are the right LENGTH (9.17 km against 9.76 observed) and simply too few - while a third of all public-transport routing requests find no service at all, which nothing has yet explained. What has genuinely improved is not the scoreboard but the instrument and the cost: the yardsticks were repaired (§9.100, §9.101, §9.130), a stopped run became citable (§9.143), and the iteration fell from 673 s to 261 s so an arm costs ~7.7 h to its gate instead of ~18. On the goal's own metric, 29 days of work has moved the number of modes inside 10% from 0 to 1.

What happened when

  1. 10 Aug (day 0): the root commit, then P1, P2 and P3 land as three pull requests in one day - a 2.3 GiB hashed data package, a 157,678-link MATSim network and a tour-based demand of 517,936 weekday agents. Nothing has run.
  2. 11 Aug: P4 opens by pointing MATSim at P3's output; all thirty assembled sets refuse to load. Three defects, and the lesson that the checks asked whether artefacts were consistent, never whether a simulator could read them.
  3. 11-16 Aug: a 73-commit branch declares every value in a registry, drives the hardcoding ledger to 0, and re-harvests OSM on a boundary-derived extent - the typed rectangle had clipped 87 of 1,500 core SA1s. Family F1 opens; the first arms run their full 1000 iterations.
  4. 18-21 Aug: ride pairing is built and immediately measured to be starved (0.104% of ride trips share an OD with a household car trip); escort binding moves pairability two orders of magnitude; walk, bike and ride become physically simulated. F4's two 1000-iteration arms produce the calibrated base - 10.65 pp MAE, infeasible - and are still the deepest runs in the project.
  5. 20-21 Aug: process hardens after five of six stacked PRs fail to reach main. Direct commits are banned, one PR per session at /handoff. This is the last day any arm runs its declared horizon.
  6. 24-27 Aug: the all-modes batch is built inert and then activated as one boundary (F6): explicit signals, tram priority, level crossings, native dwell, taxi. Every arm from here is stopped at a gate. Two document gates (currency, then figures and causes) close the drift class that had left the front door three phases stale.
  7. 28-29 Aug: twelve modes get twelve targets, and the first thing the new yardstick finds is a defect in itself - the PT composition counted another city's light rail stop, so heavy rail's apparent -1.5% fit was an artefact. Four of that session's own conclusions are corrected in the same PR.
  8. 30 Aug: the heaviest day in the project - 87 commits, eight family boundaries (F14 to F21), a demand that the committed builder could no longer reproduce, and the document restructure that puts the goal on one page behind thirteen position pages.
  9. 31 Aug - 2 Sep: the loop finally fires. F21 reads its iteration-100 gate with 0 of 12 modes inside; Opal fares are charged and F22 puts bus inside at +8.0%, the first mode ever inside; income scaling then blunts the fare and F23 reads 0 of 12 again.
  10. 3-5 Sep: the instrument turns on itself - the first whole-repository report files 26 issues, the issue gate makes an open issue a launch blocker, destination choice is constrained at both ends, and the iteration is profiled for the first time (60% of it was this project's own ride-pairing pass). F25 falsifies the demand-side explanation for ride: the seeded share rose 31% and the realised share did not move.
  11. 6-7 Sep: four physical roots are fixed with a control member each; car comes inside the band at the F28 gate for the first time in the project. Three more reports are lodged in one day, one of which measures a holdout breach in the count targets. The 2-minute-iteration directive is answered with arithmetic: no.
  12. 8 Sep (day 29): F31's gate reads 1 of 12 inside (car +5.4%), ride's mean trip length is within 6% of observation while its share is -38%, and a restored progress line reports that a third of all public-transport routing requests find no service at all. Requirement 8 is still unmeasured, across 161 runs.

Code quality by area

Six areas, each read from the flagged rows of code_metrics.json outward, each rating carrying its two strongest pieces of evidence. Ratings are not averaged across areas.

Build layer (src/build/, cities/newcastle/build/)

Depth of read. PARTIAL, declared: 9 of 36 files opened (build_manifest, build_population, build_matsim_network, build_matsim_run_inputs, build_matsim_plans, build_activity_chains, shape_tools, measure_network_factors, build_corridor_layers), ~1,450 lines read of 16,629; every other file verified only by targeted grep at the line a code_metrics row or a prior finding names. UNREAD FILES THAT CARRY A code_metrics ROW: build_landuse_parking.py (nesting 10, complexity 26), build_mode_targets.py (393-line main, 3 iterrows), build_validation_targets.py (357-line main, 2 iterrows), build_scenario_schedules.py + build_era1_reconstruction.py (12 duplicated windows, the highest pair in the repo), build_corridor_road_attributes.py, build_matsim_signals.py, build_level_crossings.py (234-line main, complexity 46), build_licence_rates.py (complexity 40, unused import), build_gtfs_extras.py (complexity 49), build_network_layers.py, gtfs_tools.py (bare except), build_data_dictionary.py (the dead module, bare except), attach_gradient.py, attach_speed_zones.py, build_params.py, det_io.py, osm_parse.py, normalise_eol.py, map_sa1_to_lga.py, measure_osm_defaults.py, build_zone_attractions.py, build_external_interaction.py, build_charging_dwell_offsets.py, build_era_feeds.py, build_scenario_configs.py, hts_purpose.py. build_matsim_plans.write_day - the repository's longest (742 lines) and most complex (151) function - was read only around :385-405 and is a named blind spot.

Two halves under one convention: src/build/ is the portable pipeline (network, population, chains, plans, run inputs, manifest) and cities/<city>/build/ holds the builders that encode one city's intervention, corridor and statistical geography. Every module resolves paths through src/city.py and values through src/registry, and the layer is pinned to the registry by check_hardcoding (0 items at HEAD, 482 declared fields, 185 source files scanned) plus check_legacy_drift (now a declared vacuous pass). The dominant structural weakness is scale rather than coupling: three modules carry 6,600 of the 16,600 lines and hold the five longest and five most complex functions in the repository, and none of the 36 files is imported by any unit test. Determinism is genuinely held on the random side (code_metrics reports 0 unseeded randomness in the build and extract layers) but not on the ordering side: build_manifest walks with an unsorted os.walk subdirectory order, and both build_manifest and build_matsim_network stamp wall-clock values into files the manifest then hashes. The registry migration is complete in the sense check_hardcoding measures - no ALL-CAPS scalar constant survives - but the same values persist one level down, inside dict(...) calls and lower-case locals that extract_legacy_constants evaluates to Ellipsis and never reports.

Run harness (run.py, src/city.py, src/run/, src/setup/, cities/newcastle/overlays/)

Depth of read. SUBSTANTIAL: 3 of 13 python files read end to end or near it - run.py (402 of 402), src/run/run_matsim.py (~1,570 of 1,632), src/run/results_store.py (462 of 462) - plus targeted reads of session_gate.py, sample_population.py, prune_run.py and run_signal_probes.py; ~2,750 lines read of 4,887. UNREAD: src/city.py (218), src/setup/bootstrap_toolchain.py (494, verified only by grep at the lines prior finding 74 names), src/setup/dump_matsim_params.py (218, unused-import row), src/run/run_failure.py (346, complexity-16 row), src/run/verify_launch.py (147), src/run/issue_gate.py (110). The 55 committed overlays under cities/newcastle/overlays/runs/ were listed, not read.

One runner owns run identity and one store owns run bytes, and both rules are enforced by construction rather than by convention: identity is the resolved parameter set plus four hashes (controler source, resolved registry values, input population, warm-start link) matched in find_completed, and every consumer resolves a run name through results_store.resolve or resolve_records. The design's strongest idea is that a run can END at three named boundaries (ran_to_last_iteration, stopped_at_gate, stopped_by_operator) and only the first is a result - and the runner gates its own arm from inside, keying the stop on a verdict FILE rather than on printed text. The weaknesses are all at the edges of that core: two modules still compose results/ paths themselves (src/run/prune_run.py:39, :112-118 and src/calibrate/calibrate.py:462-469), the store's liveness test reads only the harness pid and not the jvm_pid its own card carries, one module recompiles the signals class tree with no running-arm check that session_gate refuses for exactly that reason, and the front door's central documented promise - that the registry refuses to invent an iteration count - is no longer true.

  • Against that, run_matsim.py:1284 run() is 271 lines at complexity 45 and mixes identity resolution, directory creation, config build, JVM launch, three observers and three terminal paths in one function.

  • src/run/results_store.py walks the whole store at :391 and then each victim again at :431, and _trim_async starts that on a daemon thread concurrently with the arm it just launched, with size accounting that is not race-safe against a second harness.

Analysis and calibration (src/analyse/, src/calibrate/)

Depth of read. SUBSTANTIAL on the lane that matters: 15 of 32 files read end to end or near it - all six of src/calibrate/ (calibrate.py 560, fit.py 463, report.py 381, solve_asc_ride.py 192, measure_mode_constraints.py 194, measure_departure_constraint.py 109) plus build_fit_figures.py 673, report_mode_ridership.py 822, extract_metrics.py 506, build_status_board.py 377, iteration_trips.py 356, measure_iteration_modes.py 224, compare_runs.py 350, arm_cost.py 439, and summarise_run.py to :470 of 674; ~6,000 lines read of 11,641. UNREAD FILES THAT CARRY A code_metrics ROW: measure_corridor_composition.py (complexity 71, the highest in the repository, and a 273-line main), run_view.py (nesting 8, complexity 40, two re.compile-in-function rows), build_replay_page.py (403-line main, 0 docstrings), build_basemap.py (nesting 9 twice), decompose_ride_choice.py (nesting 7, unused import), diagnose_ride_pairing.py (complexity 28, unused import), replay_events.py (five re.compile-in-function rows), progress_digest.py (subprocess-in-loop), build_run_index.py, measure_demographic_modes.py (194-line main), measure_realisation_gap.py (itertuples), measure_ride_pairability.py, profile_run.py (DataFrame.append in loop), map_count_stations.py, corridor_market.py (complexity 30), frontage_volumes.py, mode_by_demographics.py.

A one-way pipeline with a deliberate holdout wall: run_matsim to extract_metrics (_metrics.json) to fit (_fit.json, calibration split only) to report and figures, with a parallel per-iteration path (iteration_trips to measure_iteration_modes to report_mode_ridership) that lets an arm still running be read at any iteration that wrote either a trips table or experienced plans. The holdout wall is real at the read boundary (fit.load_targets filters split == calibration and calibrate.audit_no_holdout reconciles scored plus explained equals available) and calibrate.py never opens the target file at all. The weakness is not the wall, it is the SPINE: the pipeline's own completion contract is enforced in exactly one of the seven places that present a reading. build_fit_figures._refuse_unless_ran_to_last (:153-178) and calibrate.write_constrained_base (:303-309) check completion; report_mode_ridership, build_status_board, extract_metrics, fit, calibrate's own search loop, solve_asc_ride and report.py do not, and _metrics.json and _fit.json carry the DECLARED horizon (iterations) rather than the reached one, so a stopped arm's fit block is indistinguishable from a completed arm's. Separately, the objective is a single scalar over five folded HTS categories while the board scores twelve modes: the calibration loop and the scoreboard do not measure the same thing and cannot be made to converge together.

Contract and checks (src/registry/, tests/, config/schema/, cities/newcastle/tests/, cities/newcastle/registry/, .github/workflows/)

Depth of read. PARTIAL, declared: src/registry/param_config.py read end to end (497 of 497); src/registry/__init__.py, check_city.py and check_legacy_drift.py read only at the sections prior findings name (~320 lines of 1,151); .github/workflows/test.yml and pages.yml read at their permissions and install steps; the whole registry (482 fields across 7 files) queried programmatically rather than read; check_hardcoding.py, check_city_agnostic.py, check_doc_currency.py, check_doc_shape.py and build_status_board.py --check EXECUTED at HEAD and judged on their output rather than their source. ~950 lines read of 9,758; 5 of 33 files opened. UNREAD FILES THAT CARRY A code_metrics ROW: tests/check_package.py (2,020 lines, the second-largest file in the repository, docstring coverage 0.18, a 274-line read_links), src/registry/check_hardcoding.py (1,035 lines, 4 complexity rows, 2 re.compile-in-function rows), src/registry/render_schema.py, src/registry/render_docs.py (171-line render at complexity 31), src/registry/extract_legacy_constants.py (complexity 29 - the scanner prior finding 8 is about), check_matsim_defaults.py (unused import), outputs.py, sweep_ledger.py, tests/check_doc_currency.py (5 duplicated windows, 3 re.compile rows), tests/check_doc_shape.py (4 re.compile rows), check_manifest.py, check_registry_rules.py, check_launch_refusal.py, and all 13 tests/unit modules.

The contract is unusually strong and unusually well instrumented. Values are declared once in cities/<city>/registry/ with a source class and either a sweep, a held_fixed rule or a derived_from identity; the resolver applies overlays in a fixed order and refuses an out-of-sweep or held-fixed value; param_config builds the whole MATSim config FROM the bindings so there is no template a literal could live in; and reach() proves each of the 133 bound fields moves the emitted bytes by actually nudging it. Around that sit four green gates (check_hardcoding 0, check_city_agnostic 13 of 13, check_doc_currency 0 of 46 claims drifted, check_doc_shape 0 of 5 document classes), all verified passing at HEAD in this pass, plus a green board. What the design does NOT have is a second line: the checks are strong on the half of the model that reaches a config file and blind on the half that does not. 349 of the 482 fields carry no config binding and are therefore outside reach()'s proof entirely; check_framework_is_city_free recognises a leaked city value only when it looks like a place NAME; check_no_cwd_relative_output matches a single syntactic form of one failure class; and the unit suite imports 7 of 76 src modules, so 69 modules - including every builder, the whole calibration loop and the gate reader - have no executable contract at all.

UNREAD FILES THAT CARRY A code_metrics ROW: reader_shapes.py (423 lines, complexity 24 in residence_marginals - the city's whole reader-shape adapter), extract_daytype_factors.py and extract_freight_profile.py (DataFrame.append in a loop; 12 duplicated windows between the pair), extract_hts.py (concat in loop plus 2 iterrows), extract_census.py, osm_tiles.py. No provenance_*.json was opened this pass; the four records were counted, not read. The data dictionary and the validation-target builders were not read.

Acquisition is deliberately jurisdiction-specific and lives entirely under the city, which is the right split; every download lands immutably under data/raw/ with a provenance record and every derived file is listed in a manifest with its hash and producing script. The layer's real architecture, though, is thinner than the manifest suggests: eleven of the fourteen modules have no main() and execute their whole pipeline at import, so 'the acquisition adapter' is in practice a set of scripts with no callable surface, no test seam and no way to run one stage without running all of it. Provenance is resolved by INFERENCE rather than by record - four provenance files cover fourteen raw subdirectories, and build_manifest.record_for compensates by handing an undated file its nearest ancestor directory's record - which is why 69 of the 512 manifest rows carry a blank retrieved date and 22 of those are RAW files the project treats as immutable. The one check over any of this (tests/check_manifest.py) refuses a blank LICENCE and nothing else.

MATSim extensions (src/java/, src/java_signals/)

Depth of read. PARTIAL, declared: 13 of 51 files opened, ~3,450 lines read of 15,231. Read end to end: RidePairingEngine.java (1,563), NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter.java (208), HouseholdVehicleRoster.java (161), GenericRouteTeleporter.java (133). Thread-safety, unseeded-Random, System.out, id-concat and synchronized markers were checked repository-wide by grep. UNREAD FILES THAT CARRY A code_metrics ROW: CitysimControler.java (646 lines; assemble is 503 lines, the second-longest method in the area, and it is where every binding is decided - the largest single blind spot in this area), SignalsAssemblyProbe.java (613), TramPriorityProbe.java (495), PtFareConfigGroup.java (482, 75 methods), RidePairingConfigGroup.java (482), ScatsPriorityProbe.java (381, 2 id-string-concat rows), PtFareProbe.java (341), TaxiFleetEngine.java (334), GradientLinkSpeed.java (311, the area's 2 synchronized rows), GatedSubtourProbe.java (294), SubtourChainScan.java (252, 17 System.out rows), BikeStressScoring.java (238), ActivityLinkAssigner.java (195), RemodeRestoreProbe.java (175), NestedSubtourProbe.java (153, 12 System.out rows), TolerantAgentSource.java (160), RemodeRestore.java (128), AvailabilityModesCalculator.java (132), FareChargeHandler.java (94, the area's one string-work-near-event-handler row), PtSubmodeMainModeIdentifier.java (90), and 12 further config groups.

Twenty extensions bound by one controler, all of them following the same discipline: a declared registry field reaches a MATSim ConfigGroup through param_config's binding, the class reads its own group, and 'off' reproduces stock MATSim exactly so the mechanism's effect is measurable. The heavy machinery is concentrated in the ride lane - RidePairingEngine at BeforeMobsim, JointRideEngine in the qsim, EscortCoherenceListener at replanning, GatedSubtourModeChoice in the strategy chain, HouseholdVehicleRoster and HouseholdCarDepartureHandler on vehicle identity - and that lane is where every finding below sits. Thread safety is handled by ONE declared dependency rather than by concurrent types: RUN.machine.events_synchronize_on_simsteps supplies the happens-before edge for every handler's plain maps, and src/run/run_matsim.refuse_unsafe_telemetry:82-106 refuses the illegal combination before the JVM starts. That is a defensible and well-argued trade, but the refusal names RunTelemetry only, while RidePairingEngine's inFlight and current maps and ScatsSignalController's Discharge cells depend on exactly the same edge. The deeper architectural problem is that two of these listeners write into PLAN MEMORY outside replanning and one of them keeps creating plans after innovation is switched off, which is the assumption the project's own relaxation verdict rests on.

35 candidate changes — 19 quality, 10 efficiency, 6 redundancy — sorted so that the ones which change no result come first. The column that matters is the last but one: a change that opens a comparability family is not cheaper than the arm it invalidates.

162 runs, 35 with usable timing

The simulator performance pass

Where an iteration goes, what it costs, and what one objective evaluation is worth in hours — the price list every architectural recommendation in this report has to clear.

Phase shares of a plain recurring iteration on the F31 gate arm (aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct, 25% sample, 16 threads, 40 GiB heap). The recurring iteration is 260.0 s.

The single biggest engineering win this project has made

beforeMobsimListeners — this project's own code — was 56.2% of an iteration on F23 (359 s of 639 s). It is now 1.2%. The whole of §9.142 and §9.147 went into hoisting RidePairingEngine's ~51,600 per-iteration TripRouter constructions and parallelising them. The median iteration fell 673 s → 261 s and the arm-to-gate from roughly a day to 7.66 h. Cost is genuinely no longer the binding constraint on this project; the absence of a search is.

What one objective evaluation costs

Sample × iterationsWall timeBasis
25% × 100 (the gate reading)7.66 h measuredF31 arm; band 7.5–10.8 h
25% × 250 (the GOAL horizon)18.6 h projectedat the measured 261 s recurring iteration
25% × 30022.2 h quoted, band 22.0–31.7never run
10% × 100~3.4 h projected5.0 h measured pre-repair — the projection is UNMEASURED
1% × 1000.86 h measuredmeasured unusable for scoring (§9.12: 1,032 aborted car legs vs 4 at 10%)

Shrinking the sample buys less than it looks

Pace is sub-linear in sample fraction on the current stack: two measured points (34.0 s at 1%, 260.0 s at 25%) give t = 24.6 + 935·f, a power-law exponent of 0.630. About 25 s of every iteration is fraction-independent, because the same 192,162-link network is loaded and the full transit timetable runs at every fraction — transit_capacity_scaling scales seats, not vehicles. So 25% → 10% buys roughly 2.25×, not the 6× a naive reading assumes. Whether the stack is still convex between 10% and 25% is unmeasured.

SampleEvaluations per day
25%3.1 (band 2.2–3.1)
10%7.1 — projected, not measured
1%27.9 — but not scorable

A modest four-parameter, three-point, three-round coordinate search is 36 evaluations ≈ 11.5 days of continuous machine time at 25%. The project has spent 383.2 machine hours in total, so one full search is comparable to the whole project's compute to date.

Storage. 467.2 GiB of a 500 GiB cap, 92.3% of it aborted runs, and 336.4 GiB sitting in two pre-repair arms that trimming would reclaim at once — the top row of the optimisation ledger, and it touches nothing.

The build records no time at all

NO producing script records its wall time. performance.json's build_timing field says so verbatim: 'none recorded: no producing script writes its wall time into a report or the manifest'. Verified independently this pass: none of the twenty `_*report*.json` files under cities/newcastle/ carries a wall_s, elapsed_s or duration_s key (the three that matched a grep carry typical_duration_s, act_duration_min and closed_seconds_per_site - model quantities, not clocks). MANIFEST.csv's columns are path,stage,bytes,rows,produced_by,source,source_url,licence,retrieved,sha256 - no timing column.

The 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon in GOAL.md requirement 8 is reachable in WALL CLOCK and has never been reached in fact. At the F31 arm's own measured recurring pace - 260.0 s over 98 plain iterations on aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct - 250 iterations is 66,970 s, about 18.6 h with the three one-off iterations and the twenty-minute setup; arm_cost.py quotes 22.2 h for 300 with a 22.0-31.7 h band. One arm, under a day, on the machine as it stands. What has not happened is the run: no 25% arm since F4 (21 August) has passed iteration 100, all five gate arms were stopped at their iteration-100 gate or by the operator, and requirement 8 has therefore never been measured on any stack the project now runs - while 9.7 measured both 100 and 250 too low on the stack before it. HALVING IT IS PRICED OUT ON THE ITERATION AND OPEN ON THE FRACTION. 9.155 did the arithmetic before turning a knob: of a 205.5 s profiled iteration the mobsim alone was 143 s, so zeroing every other phase still leaves the iteration above the 120 s that was asked for, and on the F31 arm the mobsim is 197.5 of 260.5 s - 75.8%. Every measured lever inside it is exhausted: 2.4x the qsim threads bought 5.6% and the mobsim is saturated at 16 (9.147); the events pool is now bracketed on both sides (1 saturated, 2 is +44.5%, 4, 12 no gain), so its 11.6% of CPU is the price of not throttling the qsim rather than waste to recover (9.155); the time-variant network is ~7-10% and NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter 8.2%, and taking all of them at their full CPU share lands near 171 s, not 130. The two structural routes that would reach it are already refused on grounds the project settled - FIFO link dynamics (23% faster in the mobsim, but a 1.25 m/s pedestrian would hold every car behind it, 9.59) and teleporting walk or bike (GOAL requirement 1). The one unmeasured lever with a plausible 2x in it is the SAMPLE FRACTION: the current stack's own two measured points give t = 24.6 + 935 x fraction, putting a 10% iteration near 118 s and a 100-iteration evaluation near 3.4 h against a measured 7.66 h, and 9.12's only measurement of what a fraction change costs the scoreboard says 10% and 25% differ by car +1.6 pp and ride -1.1 pp. That measurement is F1-era and the shared-lift bucket at 0.25 now breaks pairs at a 10% draw, so it must be re-made rather than quoted - a 0.3 h probe and one 3.4 h arm. Until it is, the honest statement is that the horizon costs 18.6-22.2 h an arm, the machine can do 3.1 such evaluations a day and cannot be parallelised (40 GiB of committed heap on a 63.5 GiB host, 40 declared threads on 24 cores, and the one-arm-at-a-time rule on top), and a 36-evaluation calibration campaign is 11.5 days - against a declared loop that can move at most four parameters and reach at most five of the twelve modes.

Testing and CI

Nine CI jobs that deliberately run nothing needing a download or a scenario, a real unit suite pointed at contracts that have previously broken — and a large uncovered surface underneath.

Workflow : conclusionRuns
test:success85
test:failure57
strip-session-ref:success31
pages-build-deployment:success18
pages:success9

200 CI runs in all: 85 test successes against 57 failures. The failures are heavily concentrated — 41 of them on one branch (praneetdhoolia/f15-choice-set-seed-bound-ride), which is a branch that was debugged in CI rather than locally, not a flaky suite.

What no test covers

69 src/ modules are imported by no unit test. Zero of the 36 build-layer modules is tested. Zero of the 14 acquisition modules is tested, and eleven of them have no main() at all, so importing one performs its downloads — there is no seam a test could use. There is no JUnit dependency, no Java test source root and no test phase anywhere in the repository: 15,231 lines of Java that decide ride pairing, signals and mode constraints are covered by twelve hand-run probe classes that assert by printing. And calibrate.py — the subject of this report's central finding — is itself in the uncovered list, which is how a fatal --set defect survives two reports.

Against that, the tests that exist are unusually well aimed: they assert contracts that have previously broken — test_fit.py::test_every_remaining_target_is_given_a_reason, test_stop_run.py asserting the gate wins over the operator, test_outputs.py validating every emitted document against config/schema.

The issue ledger

Labels across all 102 issues. `awaiting-run` is the label GOAL.md requirement 10 turns on: an issue carrying it asserts that only a measurement can move it.

The gate that is failing, and why it is weaker than it looks

The session gate is red on issues gated: 18 open issues, 17 awaiting-run, 1 blocking (#159, the manifest-lineage issue). Phase 5's assessment is that requirement 10 as implemented is satisfiable trivially and forever, because issue_gate.py tests a label string with no evidence behind it — #50 and #49 carry awaiting-run and are not measurements. Meanwhile a genuine defect (PT walk legs are teleported) is deliberately left unfiled, because filing it would block the next launch. A gate that makes filing a defect costly is selecting against being told.

The honest answer is: requirement 10 AS IMPLEMENTED can always be satisfied, and that is its weakness rather than its strength. As written in GOAL.md:56-61 the rule is 'every GitHub issue is either closed or labelled awaiting-run'. As implemented in src/run/issue_gate.py:53-55 it is a set-membership test on a label string. Applying the label costs one API call and requires no evidence, no reviewer and no record, so the gate is satisfiable in O(1) per issue no matter how many defects a report finds. It is therefore NOT the case that a report finding new defects makes the gate permanently red - a session can clear eighteen new findings in a minute by labelling them. What is at risk is the opposite: the rule's meaning. GOAL.md:57-59 says the label means 'the only thing left to do on it is a measurement that needs the run'. Nothing tests that claim, and at HEAD the label is plainly carrying issues it was not designed for - #50 'Align modelled mode distributions with demographics (age, sex, employment)' and #49 'Individualise modes' are substantive modelling work, not measurements a run makes, and both have carried awaiting-run for over a week. Meanwhile #159, which needs no run at all and is exactly the kind of thing the rule wants fixed first, is the one issue holding the gate red. So the gate is behaving correctly on the one issue it blocks and vacuously on the seventeen it passes. The structural question you asked - can requirement 10 ever be satisfied while an audit keeps finding defects - has two answers depending on which rule you mean. The LITERAL rule: yes, trivially, forever, because labelling is free. The INTENDED rule ('no unfixed defect that does not need a run stands behind an arm'): no, not while assessment continues, and it should not be - that is a correct and desirable property. An instrument that keeps finding defects and a rule that refuses to run while unfixed defects exist are in permanent tension by construction, and the tension is the point: it is what stops the project spending 22 machine hours measuring a model with a known repairable fault. The failure mode to guard against is not deadlock; it is the label becoming a way to declare the tension resolved without resolving it. Three concrete changes would make the rule mean what it says without making it unsatisfiable. First, require evidence with the label: issue_gate.py fetches the issue's comments and requires one matching a marker that names the measurement the run will make ('AWAITING-RUN: <measurement>'), so applying the label is a claim on the record rather than a click. Second, scope the gate: an issue about the manifest's lineage does not bear on a mobsim arm's validity, and blocking a physics arm on a documentation defect is the rule mis-firing - label issues with the lane they gate, and check only the lanes the run touches. Third, make the override first-class rather than exceptional: it has already been used once and the mechanism worked (it is recorded in the run and named in the brief and the board), so give it a required reason field and a count, and surface 'requirement 10 overridden N times' on the board. That converts a rule that is currently either vacuous or absolute into one that is proportionate and auditable. One further observation, because it bears on the whole loop: the project's own record already contains the strongest argument for scoping. Across 162 run directories and 29 days no arm has passed iteration 100, so requirement 8 is unmeasured; the reason each arm stops is the GOAL.md loop's 20 % stop bar, not requirement 10. Requirement 10 has never actually been the binding constraint on progress. It has cost one override and some labelling; the stop bar has cost every arm since F4.

48 projects · 12 platforms · 56 excluded

The project in its field

Every comparable city model and platform the standing reference library holds, refreshed. Not one stored fact was re-searched this pass — all 58 rows were one day old and inside their horizons — so the budget went to gaps alone.

The highest rung each of 48 project rows claims. NO project publishes the top rung — per-mode ridership for every simulated mode. Our own row is counted separately and is the only attempt at it anywhere.

Where this project sits

It is alone on the rung it has chosen, and it is not on it. Forty-eight surveyed projects, and the top rung is empty: seven make no validation claim, nine validate survey mode shares, twenty-five validate road link counts, seven validate transit ridership. Nobody publishes a per-mode ridership fit for every simulated mode. This project scores twelve modes individually against twelve targets every 100 iterations — which is genuinely further than the field goes — and reads 1 of 12 inside 10%.

Two things follow. The ambition is real and is not matched anywhere in the survey. And there is no external benchmark for it: nobody can tell this project what "good" looks like on its own metric, which is exactly why the objective function and the stopping rule have to be got right internally.

What the comparison says

  • No project in the field publishes per-mode ridership for every mode it simulates. 48 rows, and the top rung of the ladder is empty; ours is the only attempt, and it is 1 of 12 inside 10% at an iteration-100 gate that is not a result.
  • The profession's answer to 'twelve simultaneous share targets' is the ASC fixed-point loop, and its leading implementation has no working stopping rule: matsim.calibration's update is log(z_i)-log(m_i)-(log(z_0)-log(m_0)) and its check_termination carries '# TODO: not used yet'. Nobody has solved the convergence question we are asking.
  • We are the only project whose calibration search space is derived from a value registry rather than listed in the calibration script, and the only one structurally unable to read its own holdout. That is a real lead and no other row claims it.
  • We are also the most expensive per unit of information. Coordinate descent costs one full run per grid point per parameter; SPSA costs TWO runs per gradient step whatever the dimension; Cadyts costs ZERO extra runs because it corrects inside the loop; the MUM 2024 CMA-ES extension costs zero because it fits inside the iteration.
  • Not one project or framework in the survey publishes an objective-evaluation count. Nobody says how many full simulation runs their calibration took - which means our own ~140 machine hours for a 3x3x2 search has no published benchmark to be judged against.
  • BEAM is the nearest analogue: eight mode ASCs calibrated fully autonomously by Bayesian optimisation with a cheap evaluator, to a 25% L1 norm - but on a 10,000-agent scenario, not on the Bay Area model the row otherwise describes.
  • The one architecture that does not search parameters at all is Cadyts: it leaves the utility function untouched and adds a bonus to the plans whose counts match observation. It is a counts method today; nothing in the survey applies that mechanism to mode share.
  • Barcelona is the field's most honest row and the newest: a large SUMO twin with cellphone data and surveys that publishes the NEGATIVE result - 'significant challenges in capturing real-world traffic dynamics at scale despite access to substantial datasets'.

What others do that we do not

  • from: matsim.calibration (matsim-vsp) · what: an ASC fixed-point loop that moves all mode constants at once from the log-ratio of target to modelled · we lack: any ASC loop at all - our six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are unreachable from src/calibrate/calibrate.py by construction · cost to adopt: it would reopen the 8.5 decision, which exists precisely to stop ASC absorption; it is a decision, not an implementation
  • from: SPSA / W-SPSA · what: two objective measurements per gradient step regardless of dimension · we lack: a gradient step - we do axis-by-axis grid search · cost to adopt: src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 only; the registry-derived search space and the feasibility screen are unchanged
  • from: BEAM-Bayes-Opt (BOHB) · what: a cheap evaluator that scores candidates on a short run and promotes only survivors to a long one · we lack: any way to score a candidate below a full arm - every evaluation is a whole MATSim run · cost to adopt: large; it needs a defensible short-run proxy for a reading the project currently only trusts at an iteration-100 gate
  • from: Cadyts · what: correcting toward observation INSIDE the loop, by biasing plan selection instead of moving a parameter · we lack: any in-loop correction; every correction is an outer full run · cost to adopt: MATSim already ships CadytsModule; the design question is whether a mode-share analogue of a counts bonus is legitimate at all
  • from: MUM 2024 planParamCalibration (CMA-ES) · what: fitting scoring parameters inside the MATSim iteration against a ground-truth sub-population, tested for invariance across population scales · we lack: in-iteration fitting, and any test that our calibration is invariant to the 25% sample · cost to adopt: the extension is explicitly 'still under development'
  • from: GP emulator (arXiv 2203.04414) · what: deep-learning dimensionality reduction before the emulator, for a high-dimensional non-stationary simulator · we lack: any surrogate; and our loop refuses to fit more than four parameters because the objective identifies only four independent numbers · cost to adopt: it does not lift the identification limit - it makes each evaluation cheaper, not the objective richer
  • from: ARC CT-RAMP · what: one table naming every mode the model will assign, before any result · we lack: nothing - our scoreboard does this better, twelve modes each on its own basis · cost to adopt: n/a
  • from: Barcelona (SUMO) · what: publishing the negative result about its own twin · we lack: nothing structurally - 'nothing here is a result' is already the board's first line · cost to adopt: n/a

SPSA and W-SPSA for simulation calibrationsimultaneous-perturbation stochastic approximationthe general traffic-simulation calibration literature; W-SPSA in Transportation Research Part C ("W-SPSA in practice: Approximation of weight matrices and calibration of traffic simulation models")"SPSA allows for simultaneous calibration of all supply and demand parameters together"two objective measurements per gradient step, independent of the number of parametersThe single strongest argument against our coordinate descent: TWO runs per step for twelve modes, versus (grid points x free parameters) per round.

Coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (THIS PROJECT)axis-by-axis grid search with a feasibility screen; no optimiser, no gradientsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py at HEAD 6cf0ffd (read from the artefact, not searched)only registry fields that are source=assumed, carry a scalar sweep interval and are NOT held_fixed. The six mode constants (C.asc.bus -1.05, C.asc.light_rail -0.75, C.asc.rail -0.65, C.asc.walk 0.35, C.asc.cycle -1.35, C.asc.car_passenger -0.85) are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore UNREACHABLE from the loop by construction. There is NO ASC-adjustment loop in this project.calibrate.py:433 computes it explicitly: sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs. At the standing 25% sample an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall (aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct), so even a 3-point, 3-parameter, 2-round search is ~18 runs and ~140 machine hours.It is the only method in this list whose search space is derived from a value registry rather than listed in the calibration script, and the only one that is structurally unable to read a holdout. It is also the most expensive per unit of information: one full run per grid point per parameter, against SPSA's two per gradient step and Cadyts' zero.

Two findings the survey produced that are worth more than the table

No project or framework anywhere in the survey publishes an objective-evaluation count. The cost of calibration is the field's unreported number. This report's Phase 3 measures ours at 7.66 h, which makes this project — accidentally — better placed than the field to reason about whether a search is affordable.

The leading open implementation has no working stopping rule. matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes the ASC update verbatim as math.log(z_i) - math.log(m_i) - (math.log(z_0) - math.log(m_0)) under Optuna, and its TerminationCondition.check_termination carries # TODO: not used yet with no default learning-rate scheduler. The standard answer to this project's problem is standard, widely used, and unfinished.

2026-09-08

79 factors across eleven layers

The factor ledger

Every factor the research says bears on how people and goods decide to move, with its status in this model re-read at HEAD by grep — never carried forward, because the model moves weekly and a carried status is a wrong status.

IN · PARTIAL · INERT (declared in the registry, read by nothing) · ASC (folded into a mode constant) · OUT. Against the 7 September baseline of 37/27/2/1/5: not one of the 72 carried-over factors changed class — the whole delta is the seven rows added this pass.

That stability is itself a result. Between two reports a day apart, spanning one full comparability family and a gate firing, no factor's coverage changed. The model's behavioural surface is not what has been moving; the plumbing around it is.

What would move the scoreboard

#FactoridStatusModeDeviationWhy
1Crowding (seated / standing)E11PARTIALheavy_rail+247.2%Still the largest deviation on the board and still without a brake. Capacity binds physically - all four fleet types are patched from published seated/standing figures at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:270-279 - but C.crowding.seated_multiplier (1.0) and standing_multiplier (1.45) carry no matsim_param and reach only params/C1_parameters.json through src/build/build_params.py:101-102, and build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1212 lists them as not representable. The literature is quantified and unambiguous (a standing multiplier around 1.4-1.5 on in-vehicle time), the coefficients are already declared with sweeps, and neither the demand nor the network moves.
2Identifiability under many simultaneous targetsI9INall twelvenine of twelve outside 10%NEW THIS PASS, and it is the constraint every other recommendation must pass. The loop is correct to refuse more than CAL.objective.independent_targets = 4 free parameters (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:399, :429), but four independent numbers cannot move nine deviations. The published route is to buy independent targets of a DIFFERENT kind: CAL.objective.include_counts is false, and the disclosed rail and tram boardings that already back the heavy_rail and light_rail targets are scored but not in the objective. Each such target added is one more parameter the loop may legitimately move - and the numbers are already in the package.
3Surrogate / metamodel-assisted calibrationI8OUTall twelveheavy_rail +247.2%, taxi +178.4%, bike +147.4%NEW THIS PASS. The single largest structural gap between this model and the field's current practice on the exact problem this project has: an objective nobody can afford to evaluate. Osorio's analytical metamodel reached its best point on a 30,000-dimension Salt Lake City calibration in ONE simulation iteration (nRMSE 120% to 32%, against 117% for SPSA over 15); a random-forest surrogate under Bayesian optimisation fitted 477 behavioural parameters of SimMobility MT for Tallinn in about 150 evaluations, AGAINST AGGREGATE MODE SHARES - which is precisely this city's data class. Nothing about the demand, the network or the Java changes.
4Automatic calibration: the search algorithm and its evaluation budgetI7INall twelvenine of twelve outside 10%NEW THIS PASS. The loop exists and has never been run: coordinate descent at 3 points x 4 parameters x 3 rounds = at most 36 full MATSim runs (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:433). Coordinate descent is the weakest member of the published family for a stochastic, expensive objective, and the literature's summary of the budget problem is exactly this project's: computational budgets are one to two orders of magnitude below the problem dimension, and general-purpose algorithms are not designed to be stopped that early. Choosing the algorithm is cheap; running it is the cost.
5Reliability and headwayE12INERTbus+54.6%The two coefficients are declared with values and sweeps (C.time_weights.beta_headway 0.5, beta_reliability 1.3), are written into params/C1_parameters.json by src/build/build_params.py:99-100, and carry no matsim_param and no reader in the run - confirmed again at HEAD. Bus at +54.6% and light_rail at -47.2% are the two modes whose share the literature says headway and reliability weights move most, and both readings are wrong in the direction an absent headway penalty predicts.
6ASC calibration methodI6PARTIALbus+54.6%Six of the seven mode constants are assumed priors held fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are unreachable from the loop by construction, while the objective is mode share ALONE (CAL.objective.components = {mode_share.mean_abs_pp: 1.0}, include_counts false). The practice standard for exactly this situation is the ln(observed/modelled) adjustment to a plus-or-minus one percentage point threshold - with the profession's own warning that it is a last resort because a constant absorbs every omitted variable, which is why 8.5 froze them. The tension is real and should be decided on the record rather than left implicit.
7Taxi / rideshare: wait, fleet, refusal, surgeE17PARTIALtaxi+178.4%The second-largest deviation on the board, and it grew since the last pass (+105.6% to +178.4%). The fleet is finite and refusal is physical (src/java/citysim/TaxiFleetEngine.java:31,62; B.taxi.fleet_size = 800, max_wait_min = 20.0), and metered fares are wired - but surge is absent outright (grep returns nothing in src) and the registry itself records surge as unknowable and unmodelled. A mode carrying 178% too many trips with no price response to demand is the shape that missing surge predicts.
8Bike: stress (traffic), gradient, e-bikeE14INbike+147.4%Bike is IN and physical - felt-time stress in both the router (src/java/citysim/BikeStressDisutility.java:27) and scoring, gradient through GradientLinkSpeed - and still 147% over. What is missing is on the OTHER side of the row: e-bike does not exist as a vehicle type anywhere (the vehicle-type row is OUT at HEAD), and bicycle ownership at 0.493 gates availability but nothing gates the trip LENGTH distribution the stress model is drawn over. The literature's stress magnitudes are already in the registry with sweeps, so this is a parameter question, not an acquisition.
9Equilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?H6PARTIALride-38.0%NEW THIS PASS. Relaxation is judged only by aggregate mode-share drift (RUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5, src/analyse/summarise_run.py:75-84) and no equilibrium gap is computed anywhere at HEAD. A flat share is compatible with a large gap, so an arm can read relaxed while agents still have score to gain - a live candidate explanation for readings that sit still and wrong through the innovation-off tail (ride -38.0%, light_rail -47.2%). src/analyse/decompose_ride_choice.py already measures a per-agent score gap for ride, so the instrument exists in miniature.
10Estimating choice parameters from aggregate data onlyI10PARTIALbus+54.6%NEW THIS PASS, and it settles a standing worry with evidence rather than assertion: the aggregate-only NSW HTS is NOT a bar to fitting a large behavioural parameter set. Tallinn fitted 477 parameters against the modal share of the whole population; the ActivitySim ASC adjustment needs nothing but shares; BLP recovers heterogeneous tastes from shares alone given instruments. This model currently uses the aggregate route for exactly ONE constant (src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py, car passenger, reported as a constraint). The other six are frozen while four modes sit far outside 10%.

The top mover has been the top mover for four reports

Crowding (E11) is PARTIAL against heavy rail at +247.2%. Capacity binds physically — all four fleet types are patched from published seated and standing figures at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:270-279 — but C.crowding.seated_multiplier (1.0) and standing_multiplier (1.45) carry no matsim_param, reach only params/C1_parameters.json, and build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1212 lists them as not representable. Heavy rail therefore has no brake of any kind: an unlimited number of agents can board a full train at no disutility. This is the single clearest case in the repository where a mode's deviation is a missing mechanism rather than a mis-set taste parameter — and it is why an ASC loop must not be allowed to touch heavy rail's constant.

A1Residential location (fixed from census)INsrc/build/build_population.py:244 places every synthetic person in an SA1 against D1_zone_attractions_SA1.csv; cities/newcastle/build/map_sa1_to_lga.py carries the SA1->LGA join; B.population.build_sample_share = 1.0Residential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the built-environment effect and mis-states only the self-selected minority.Nothing directly - homes are fixed from the census and are not a free parameter. A2Workplace locationPARTIALDestinations are drawn from a solved gravity decay over D1 attractions (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:410, :253) and the external tier from B.external.commute_share_to_core (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:1950); there is NO modelled-vs-census journey-to-work flow check and no inter-LGA commute constraint - STATUS.md names "inter-LGA commute flows" as an open assessment findingWorkplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.Commute distance is what separates a car trip from a walk trip. Across 19 major cities in 13 countries and 6 continents (8 low-and-middle-income, 11 high-income), females are more likely than males to walk in every city - on average 23% more likely - and on average 6% more likely to use public transport, while the relation REVERSES for cycling, where women are typically about half as likely to cycle as men; in high-cycling cities the two genders are equally likely, and in Berlin, Munich and Hamburg women cycle more than men. The gap is age-dependent: among children under 16 the metrics are often equal, and the disparity widens with age. On age itself, older travellers drive, walk and take taxis and make little use of bicycles or rideshare, car use falls and dependence on transit rises as the ability to drive falls, and older women are the group most likely to use public transport; an urban Italian study puts men at ~1.5x the odds of choosing a private car over an active mode. Critically, travel is generally INELASTIC with respect to every built-environment measure.The built form is the standard explanation for why an inner suburb walks and an outer one drives. About 50% of trips were within 30 s and about 90% within 5 minutes of the shortest-time route, so the deviation is wide in route space and narrow in time. A Chongqing trajectory study of 2,860 private-car trips by ~400 drivers puts the shortest-path match at ~67% under a looser matching rule. F2Parking search and occupancyPARTIALSearch time IS scored per zone (A.parking.search_time_representation = "scoring", src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:940-949); but occupancy is static - A.parking.occupancy_profile (24 hourly values) and A.parking.capacity_default reach only cities/newcastle/build/build_landuse_parking.py:305-313, and no bay is consumed or queued for in the mobsimCruising for parking is a measured, large phenomenon: 3.5-14 minutes to find a curb space in congested downtowns, 8-74% of the traffic stream cruising (over 70% in recent work), and search time up to 40% of total travel time. F4Ride pairing / matchingINcitysim.RidePairingEngine with B.ride.pairing_window_min = 15.0, B.ride.bound_pairing_window_min, B.ride.pairing_rule, B.ride.max_passengers_per_vehicle, B.ride.remode_unpaired and B.ride.unpaired_fallback; the window is bounds-checked against its own sweep at src/analyse/measure_ride_pairability.py:209-241Two literatures answer this and they are not the same. G4Queueing model and passingINRUN.qsim.link_dynamics = "PassingQ" with RUN.qsim.vehicles_source = "modeVehicleTypesFromVehiclesData"; storage scaling at RUN.sample.storage_capacity_exponent (src/run/run_matsim.py:394-400) and flowCapacityFactor = RUN.sample.fraction (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1280)MATSim's default link is a spatial FIFO queue with two parameters, flow capacity and storage capacity, and no intra-link interaction; the passing-queue extension lets faster vehicles overtake slower ones within a link so that, when walking and cycling are simulated on the road, pedestrians and cyclists do not block cars in the queue - the AToM Melbourne model documents this as the required setting for a multimodal network.PassingQ is what lets a bike and a truck share a link without one blocking the other, so it bears on bike +147.4% and truck alike. idFactorStatusProof at HEADWhat the research saysWhat it would move
H1Utility form (Charypar-Nagel scoring)INC.scoring.performing_utils_per_h, marginal_utility_of_traveling, monetary_distance_rate and marginal_utility_of_money assembled at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1081-1198; RUN.scoring.brain_exp_beta and RUN.scoring.learning_rate set the logit scale; the config is BUILT from the declared matsim_param bindings by src/registry/param_config.py, so a literal has nowhere to liveMATSim's scoring is the Charypar-Nagel form: plan utility is the sum of activity utilities plus travel disutilities, with activity utility beta_dur * t_typ * ln(t_dur / t_0) - marginal utility of duration against a typical duration and a minimal duration below which utility is negative - and leg score built from a mode constant, a marginal disutility of travel duration, and a marginal disutility of distance. Under iteration the population's average plan score stabilises at a point where individuals cannot unilaterally improve.The utility form is the frame every deviation is expressed in. It is correctly and completely wired; the gaps in this ledger are missing TERMS (crowding, headway, per-purpose VOT), not a missing form.
H2Heterogeneity / value-of-time segmentsPARTIALIncome heterogeneity IS per person (citysim.IncomeScoringConfigGroup scales each agent's marginalUtilityOfMoney by (average/personal)^C.income.exponent, exponent 1.0) and subpopulations carry their own scoring; but the six C.vot.by_purpose values collapse to one trip-weighted average (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1209-1211), so purpose segmentation is absentHeterogeneity in the value of time is real and income-driven, with an income elasticity of VTTS of about 0.67-0.80 - below the unity convention. MATSim's own agent-heterogeneity work treats per-agent parameter variation as a first-class scenario feature rather than an extension.A single VOT segment is why bus (+54.6%) and heavy_rail (+247.2%) both overshoot at once: the model has one traveller type and it is time-rich. The six declared values and the sweeps already exist.
H3Choice-set generation and mode availabilityPARTIALcitysim.AvailabilityModesCalculator and citysim.GatedSubtourModeChoice gate availability per person and per subtour, and B.mode.seed_method = "full_choice_set" seeds the whole set; BUT RUN.mode_choice.modes has only six of the twelve - [car, ride, pt, bike, walk, taxi] - so motorbike, truck and freight are carved deterministically and are never chosenThe choice set in an agent-based model is generated, not enumerated: MATSim's SubtourModeChoice changes the mode of all legs of one randomly chosen subtour to a randomly chosen alternative, and offers a mode only where the choice would not require a resource to appear out of thin air - chain-based modes assume one resource per mode, initially at home. The discrete-mode-choice contrib exists for scenarios needing an explicit, estimable choice model instead.Six modes compete for 100% of the choosable mass, and four of them (walk -11.1%, taxi +178.4%, bike +147.4%, bus +54.6%) overshoot while two undershoot (car +5.4%, ride -38.0%). A choice set of six modes cannot make a motorbike absorb any of that. This is the structural reason the residual has nowhere to go.
H4Learning, replanning, plan memory, innovation switch-offINRUN.replanning.weights = {ChangeExpBeta 0.7, ReRoute 0.15, SubtourModeChoice 0.1, TimeAllocationMutator 0.05}; RUN.replanning.max_agent_plan_memory = 8; RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation = 0.8 with the drift read at src/analyse/summarise_run.py:378-384The distinction that governs convergence: while innovation is switched on - new routes, new times - the result is NOT truly stationary; if innovation is switched off the process is stationary but limited to the plans each agent holds at that moment. The plan set is the agent's choice set, and MATSim's recommended control is fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation rather than a per-strategy disable iteration. ADDED 8 September 2026: what the loop is converging TO is stated by MATSim's own equilibrium work - an approximate minimisation of an equilibrium gap that measures, per agent, how much it could improve by changing its plan while all others keep theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium'. Reproducible computation of a point equilibrium is named as the single most important advantage of the four-step model that MATSim does not have by default. See the new factor 'Equilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?'.Every mode reading on the board is taken at iteration 20 of a stopped arm - well inside the innovating phase.
