H5LLM-driven agentsOUTgrep -riE "\bllm\b|language model|gpt" over src returns no agent code (the only "gpts" hit is a GeoDataFrame variable at src/build/build_activity_chains.py:2551)Two 2025-2026 results now bracket this lane. On the optimistic side, GATSim integrates LLM-powered generative agents - hierarchical memory, multi-modal retrieval, planning, reactive and reflection processes, diverse socioeconomic profiles and lifelong learning - into an urban mobility environment, and reports validation at microscopic and macroscopic levels, claiming agents 'perform competitively with human annotators in role-playing scenarios' while 'naturally producing realistic macroscopic traffic patterns'; its abstract states no accuracy figure, no real city and no cost per agent-day. On the sceptical side, the first systematic evaluation against observed mobility (2026) measures AgentSociety and CitySim over Greater Paris (3,337 residents, 7 days) and Shanghai (58,502 users, 10 days) and separates 'face validity' from 'objective mobility realism': AgentSociety's travel-distance error is a Wasserstein distance of 14.83 plus or minus 0.35 km and CitySim's 7.53 plus or minus 1.67 km, with origin-destination similarity at a common-part-of-commuters of 0.138 plus or minus 0.018; trip-duration error is 24.41 plus or minus 0.24 minutes and dwell-time error 3.96 plus or minus 0.12 hours, against reference-sample variability of 0.29 minutes and 0.26 hours. Activity PROPORTIONS come out well (Jensen-Shannon divergence 0.0296) while activity SEQUENCES do not (0.1125), and mobility diversity is 'unstable across default prompting configurations'. The finding to carry: LLM agents reproduce qualitative mobility laws and aggregate activity mixes, and miss individual spatial behaviour by one to two orders of magnitude more than sampling error.Nothing on the current board. The surveyed field's LLM lane publishes no validated city, so its absence costs this project no rung on the validation ladder.
H6Equilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?PARTIALThe loop runs (RUN.replanning.weights = {ChangeExpBeta 0.7, ReRoute 0.15, SubtourModeChoice 0.1, TimeAllocationMutator 0.05}, RUN.replanning.max_agent_plan_memory = 8, RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation = 0.8, with RUN.scoring.brain_exp_beta setting the logit scale), but convergence is judged ONLY by aggregate mode-share drift: RUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5 over RUN.relaxation.settle_margin_iterations, read at src/analyse/summarise_run.py:75-84 and plotted by src/analyse/progress_digest.py:10. No equilibrium gap is computed anywhere - a grep for the greedo/emulation contribs and for a scenario gap measure over src, src/java and src/java_signals at HEAD returns only unrelated uses of the word; src/analyse/decompose_ride_choice.py:10 measures a per-agent score gap to the best RIDE plan, a one-mode diagnostic rather than a scenario equilibrium gap.MATSim's mobsim/scoring/replanning loop is a Monte-Carlo co-evolutionary search, not a solved fixed point, and its own authors say so. Floetteroed's statement of the position is the clearest available: the assignment relies on approximate minimisation of an EQUILIBRIUM GAP measuring, for every agent, how much that agent could improve its score by changing its plan if all other agents kept theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium', and the method 'aims to reduce the gap in subsequent MATSim iterations, steering the simulation process towards a state that has a low gap, and hence may be deemed to be near an equilibrium point'. He names the reproducible computation of point equilibria as 'the single most important advantage' of the traditional four-step / static-assignment model - an advantage MATSim does not have by default - and supplies the emulation and greedo contribs that add gap minimisation to the loop, illustrated on a multimodal Greater Stockholm scenario with all-day route, departure-time and mode choice. The wider theory agrees: MATSim targets a STOCHASTIC user equilibrium (minimum PERCEIVED cost) rather than a Nash equilibrium; best-response dynamics carry no convergence guarantee, though if they converge they converge to an equilibrium. No published convergence rate exists for a multimodal MATSim scenario: relaxation is asserted by observation, not proved.It reframes the horizon question rather than one mode's number. A flat mode share is compatible with a large equilibrium gap, so an arm can look relaxed at RUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5 while agents are still leaving score on the table - a live candidate explanation for readings that sit still and wrong across the innovation-off tail: ride -38.0% and light_rail -47.2% at iteration 100 of the F31 arm. src/analyse/decompose_ride_choice.py already measures a per-agent score gap for ride, so the instrument exists in miniature; extending it to a scenario-level gap needs no new data and no change to the demand or the network.
H7In-loop parameter estimation from a ground-truth subpopulationOUTNo ground-truth subpopulation and no in-loop estimator exist at HEAD. RUN.replanning.subpopulations = ['person', 'external', 'freight'] and RUN.replanning.strategy_subpopulations = {'SubtourModeChoice': ['person']} (cities/newcastle/registry/RUN_execution.json:309-322); grep -riE 'KeepLastSelected|ground.truth|groundtruth' and grep -riE 'CMA-ES|cma_es' over src, cities/newcastle/build, src/java and src/java_signals return nothing. The data precondition also fails: src/analyse/measure_demographic_modes.py:15 records that the NSW HTS tables carry no unit records to pin a survey agent's plan to.An architecture that avoids the outer loop entirely: estimate the utility parameters INSIDE the simulation, against a subpopulation of real survey respondents whose observed plans are pinned. The MATSim planParamCalibration extension does exactly that - a designated subpopulation carries its surveyed plan under the KeepLastSelected strategy so those plans are the ground truth, the remaining agents generate alternatives by the ordinary strategies, and CMA-ES maximises a logit-like log-likelihood over the planCalcScore parameters (mode constants, marginal utility of travelling, of distance and of money, daily monetary constants, typical and minimal activity durations, line-switch, waiting, late-arrival and early-departure terms) at each MATSim iteration, writing the result back into the config for the next one. It stops on a designated iteration or on convergence, the default being an average estimated difference below 0.001. Tested on a 2023 street-interview trip-diary survey plus mobile-location commuting arrays at 100 m grid accuracy, the maximum log-likelihood is stable over twenty MATSim iterations and essentially unchanged whether the calibration population is respondents alone or respondents plus 100k, 300k, 600k or one million commuting records - the claimed proof that the estimator is auto-adaptive to population scale. The price of the architecture is exactly the data an aggregate-only city lacks: the likelihood's observations are unit-record plans.Nothing today, and the row exists to say exactly why. Every parameter this architecture would estimate is one this model currently asserts - the six assumed C.asc.* constants, C.vot.by_purpose collapsed to one trip-weighted 16.96 AUD/h at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1209-1211, the C.time_weights.* family - and it would estimate them at ZERO extra simulation cost, which at this project's arm prices is the whole difficulty. It is blocked on one acquisition and one only: unit-record trip diaries. That is the same blocker already tracked for machine-learned choice models, which makes the TfNSW HTS unit-record request the highest-leverage data item outstanding rather than a nicety.
H8Machine-learned choice models in place of a hand-specified utilityOUTNo machine-learned component of any kind exists at HEAD: grep -riE 'sklearn|torch|tensorflow|xgboost|neural' over src, cities/newcastle/build, src/java and src/java_signals returns nothing. The utility is hand-specified Charypar-Nagel scoring assembled from declared registry fields at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1081-1198, with the mode constants at :1088-1105.Neural choice models beat multinomial logit on prediction and lose on the quantity a twin is actually scored on. A utility-informed neural network trained on 14,671 trips from the 2017 US National Household Travel Survey for California reached 89.03% mode-choice accuracy, the highest in its benchmark against MNL and other classifiers; alternative-specific-utility deep networks (ASU-DNN) and residual-logit hybrids (ResLogit) are likewise consistently more accurate than MNL on the same data. The published caution is sharper than the accuracy claim: the models with the best DISAGGREGATE predictive performance - gradient-boosted trees and random forests - give POORER estimates of behavioural indicators and of AGGREGATE MODE SHARES than deep neural networks and than plain multinomial logit. Every method in this family is estimated on unit-record choice observations with the alternatives' attributes attached; none can be fitted to a published aggregate share table, and none has been shown to sit inside an equilibrium loop where the attributes of the alternatives are themselves simulation outputs.Nothing that could be adopted here, and the literature says so twice over. It needs unit-record choices this city does not have (src/analyse/measure_demographic_modes.py:15), and its own benchmark shows the most accurate learners degrade exactly the statistic this board is scored on - aggregate mode share, where nine of twelve modes are outside 10%. The transferable lesson is negative and worth stating: the machine learning that would help this project is the SURROGATE of the simulator (row I8), not a learned replacement for the traveller.

I10Estimating choice parameters from aggregate data onlyPARTIALThe aggregate route is used, but not as an estimator. The objective is aggregate mode share alone (CAL.objective.components = {mode_share.mean_abs_pp: 1.0}, cities/newcastle/registry/CAL_calibration.json, consumed by src/calibrate/calibrate.py) and ONE constant is solved from an aggregate observation - src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py:1-31 solves C.asc.car_passenger to reproduce the published passenger:driver ratio and reports it as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The other six C.asc.* values remain assumed priors held fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are unreachable from the loop by construction (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:13-18). There is no ASC adjustment loop, no share inversion and no moment estimator. The data constraint is recorded at src/analyse/measure_demographic_modes.py:15 - the NSW HTS tables 'carry NO demographic column' - with src/analyse/extract_metrics.py:8-16 working from the published MODE_SHARE, TRIP_AVG_DISTANCE and TRIP_AVG_TIME tables.Three distinct families exist for a city with no unit-record survey. (1) AGGREGATE ASC ADJUSTMENT, the practice standard: iteratively add the log ratio of observed to modelled share to each mode constant, re-run, repeat until the split is inside a stated threshold, commonly plus or minus one percentage point; ActivitySim adjusts tour-level and trip-level constants together with the same increment because tour mode conditions trip mode. The profession's own validation manual warns that revising constants is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted, because a constant absorbs every omitted variable. (2) BLP-STYLE DEMAND INVERSION: a contraction mapping inverts observed market shares to implied mean utilities and GMM on instrumented moments recovers heterogeneous taste coefficients 'from only aggregate market-share data', removing the IIA restriction on substitution; the requirement is instruments with genuine cross-market variation, which a single-city model does not naturally possess. (3) SURROGATE-ASSISTED SIMULATION-BASED ESTIMATION against aggregate benchmarks: the Tallinn SimMobility work fitted 477 behavioural parameters entirely against 'aggregate benchmarks (e.g., the modal share of the whole population)' and names disaggregate data only as future work - a direct feasibility proof that unit records are not a precondition for fitting a large behavioural parameter set.It is the honest ceiling on what this city's data can identify, and it says the ceiling has not been reached. Six mode constants are frozen at assumed priors while bus reads +54.6%, light_rail -47.2%, heavy_rail +247.2% and ferry -65.6% - four deviations an aggregate ASC adjustment is designed to close, and that DECISIONS.md 8.5 currently forbids the loop from touching. Nothing new has to be acquired: the published aggregate shares that would drive the adjustment are already the targets.

What the guidance does not describe is enforcement - no surveyed practice makes the holdout unreadable by construction.Nothing on the board today - the holdout opens once, at the end (STATUS P5). It is what will make any eventual reading credible, and it is enforced in two independent places rather than by convention.
I3Convergence criterionINRUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5 and RUN.relaxation.settle_margin_iterations read at src/analyse/summarise_run.py:75-84 and plotted by src/analyse/progress_digest.py:10Convergence in an iterative agent model has a precise meaning and a precise trap: the process is not stationary while innovation runs, and is stationary after switch-off only within the plans agents already hold. Empirically, between-seed variation in link loads dominates the variation between the last two iterations within one seed, so a within-run stability test alone is not evidence of convergence.The board reads at iteration 20 of a stopped arm because no arm since family F4 has reached its gate. The criterion is wired; what is missing is a run that survives long enough to test it against the GOAL.md 250-iteration requirement.
I4Replication across seeds / run-to-run noisePARTIALE.replication.n_replications = 30 is declared and reaches cities/newcastle/build/build_scenario_configs.py:40,172; RUN.machine.seed is declared "held at the master seed unless replications are being drawn" and was exercised once, by the phys1000_arm_b_25pct overlay, whose own record says "no seed-variance measurement exists yet"Random seeds move agent-based results materially: across 100 seeds of one MATSim scenario, relative errors of up to 10% occur even on links with large volumes, and the variation between seeds largely dominates the variation between the two last iterations within a seed. Aggregate travel times are robust after one iteration, but disaggregate results needed about 31 simulations on average to reach a robust mean.EVERY deviation on the board is quoted without an error bar. I5Sensitivity sweepsINEvery field carries a sweep, a held_fixed rule or a derived_from identity or the schema rejects it. Re-run read-only at HEAD: check_hardcoding.py reports 482 declared fields over 185 source files and TOTAL 0 items, with section 7 proving 133 of 133 bound fields reach the config by being nudged, and section 1 listing 4 declared-ahead-of-consumer fields each naming its issue (B.activity.weekend_to_weekday, B.counts.vehicles_per_car_leg, B.counts.vehicles_per_ride_leg, C.constraint.passenger_per_driver).The recommended method for agent-based models is variance-based global sensitivity analysis: because ABMs are non-linear, Sobol' indices decompose the output variance into first-order and total contributions of each parameter and its interactions, sampled with Sobol' sequences over the input space; one-at-a-time sweeps are the local, linear special case and miss interactions.This is the control that makes every other row in this ledger actionable: no lever named here is a number typed into a script. It is the project's strongest process claim.
I6ASC calibration methodPARTIALC.asc.car_driver (0.0, the reference), car_passenger, bus, light_rail, rail, walk, cycle map to MATSim modeParams constants at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1088-1105, with per-submode constants under RUN.routing.pt_submode_scoring; src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py solves the ride ASC. But CAL.objective.components = {mode_share.mean_abs_pp: 1.0} and CAL.objective.include_counts = False - the objective is mode share ONLYThe practice standard is an iterative adjustment rather than an estimation: compare the modelled split to the observed split, add the log ratio of observed to modelled share to each mode constant, re-run, and repeat until the split is inside a stated error threshold, commonly plus or minus one percentage point; ActivitySim applies the same increment to tour-level and trip-level constants together because tour mode conditions trip mode. The profession's own validation guidance is explicit that this is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted - 'the constants can easily be revised so that modeled mode shares match targets', which is precisely the danger, since a constant absorbs every omitted variable and every supply error along with the genuine preference. In an agent-based model the problem is harder than in a four-step model because the attributes of the alternatives are outcomes of the simulation, so the constants cannot be estimated by ordinary maximum likelihood at all; the MATSim-native answer (Rakow and Nagel 2024) is a simulation-based calibration that fine-tunes the ASCs to align simulated mode shares with reference data, and eqasim does the same through boptx.Ten of twelve modes are outside 10% and eight past the 20% stop bar, so the ASCs are the fastest lever on the board by construction. The risk is the same one that makes them fast: with counts out of the objective and no crowding or headway term, an ASC fit will absorb specification error as preference.
I7Automatic calibration: the search algorithm and its evaluation budgetINCoordinate descent over registry-derived free parameters: CAL.search.points_per_parameter = 3, CAL.search.max_rounds = 3, CAL.search.convergence_delta = 0.25 read at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:400-402; the budget is computed at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:433 (evals = sum(len(grid(p, ppp)) for p in free) * max_rounds) and announced at :434 as 'coordinate descent'; the loop itself is src/calibrate/calibrate.py:518-527. NO surrogate, no SPSA, no CMA-ES and no Bayesian optimisation exist at HEAD: grep -riE 'surrogate|metamodel|emulator|gaussian.process|random.forest|kriging|SPSA|CMA-ES|scipy.optimize' over src, cities/newcastle/build, src/java and src/java_signals returns nothing.Calibrating a microsimulation is a black-box, stochastic, expensive simulation-based optimisation problem, and the published methods separate by how many simulation evaluations they can afford. SPSA (simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation) is the field's workhorse because it costs only two simulation evaluations per gradient estimate whatever the dimension, and W-SPSA extends it with a weight matrix; but it is built for asymptotic guarantees rather than early termination, and under a small budget it barely moves - on a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions SPSA took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 117% over fifteen simulation iterations, while a metamodel method reached 32%. Evolutionary strategies (CMA-ES, xNES) and finite-difference gradient approximation (FDSA, SPSA) are what the MATSim/eqasim calibration framework boptx implements. The cross-entropy method is a Monte-Carlo importance-sampling search and is the most expensive family: one published SUMO calibration of a three-intersection model spent 98,304 simulation evaluations. Bayesian optimisation over a surrogate is the current answer for a small budget (see the surrogate row). The field states its own constraint plainly: computational budgets in the literature are 'one to two orders of magnitude lower than the problem dimension', and general-purpose algorithms 'are designed for asymptotic performance guarantees and are not designed to be terminated with such few function evaluations'.Nothing on its own - it is the machine that would move everything else, and it has never been run. At HEAD the loop is a coordinate-descent grid whose budget is at most 3 points x 4 parameters x 3 rounds = 36 full MATSim runs (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:433). Nine of twelve modes sit outside 10% (heavy_rail +247.2%, taxi +178.4%, bike +147.4%, ferry -65.6%, bus +54.6%, light_rail -47.2%, ride -38.0%, motorbike +13.7%, walk -11.1%) with no automated search ever executed against them, and at the F31 arm's measured pace 36 runs is a budget nobody has priced. The literature's answer to exactly this bind is the surrogate row below.
I8Surrogate / metamodel-assisted calibrationOUTNo surrogate, emulator, metamodel or learned response surface exists anywhere in the repository at HEAD: grep -riE 'surrogate|metamodel|emulator|gaussian.process|random.forest|kriging' and grep -riE 'sklearn|torch|tensorflow|xgboost|neural' over src, cities/newcastle/build, src/java and src/java_signals both return nothing. Every objective evaluation in src/calibrate/calibrate.py:522 is a full MATSim run.The canonical line is Osorio's metamodel simulation-based optimisation: replace the expensive simulated objective with an analytical network model plus a low-order statistical correction, then solve a sequence of cheap analytical problems, so that good points are found from the first iterations without a large initial sample. Its strongest published demonstration is a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions, where within ONE simulation iteration the linear-metamodel method took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 32%, against 48% for a tailored linear-assignment method and 117% for SPSA, all inside a fifteen-simulation-iteration budget - and 'thereafter there is not much improvement within such few iterations', i.e. nearly all the gain arrives at the first evaluation. The second family is machine-learned rather than analytical: a random-forest surrogate driving Bayesian optimisation calibrated 477 behavioural parameters of the SimMobility MT activity-based model for Tallinn, and did so against AGGREGATE benchmarks ('the modal share of the whole population'), reaching 4% error on the total number of trips and an average origin-destination error of 15.92 vehicles per day. That paper states no prior work had calibrated as many as 477 parameters and that existing rigorous methods 'do not consider more than a few dozen of parameters (the maximum number being 98)'.It is the cheapest route to moving the whole board at once rather than one mode at a time. Every deviation on the scoreboard - heavy_rail +247.2%, taxi +178.4%, bike +147.4%, ferry -65.6%, bus +54.6%, light_rail -47.2%, ride -38.0% - is a target of one objective that has never been optimised, because each evaluation is a multi-hour run and the loop can afford 36 of them (src/calibrate/calibrate.py:433). The Tallinn result is the direct precedent: 477 behavioural parameters fitted against AGGREGATE mode shares, which is exactly the data class this city has, in about 150 evaluations. Nothing about the demand, the network or the Java would change, and the data is already in the package.
I9Identifiability under many simultaneous targetsINThe loop counts independent numbers and refuses: CAL.objective.independent_targets = 4 (cities/newcastle/registry/CAL_calibration.json, source 'derived') is read at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:399 and enforced at :420-431, exiting with 'refusing to fit %d parameters to %d independent numbers: that is not a calibration'. The rule is stated at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:20-23: 'The objective contains four independent numbers (five HTS mode shares that sum to one).'A parameter set is identified only if distinct parameter values produce distinguishable outputs on the targets you actually hold, and the simulation-calibration literature is explicit that when a model is over-parametrised relative to its targets, 'non-identifiability can arise, making it theoretically impossible to locate the true parameter value'. The published remedy is not a better optimiser but a different answer: report an ELIGIBILITY SET - the set of all parameter values whose simulated outputs match the data - constructed to carry rigorous frequentist guarantees, extended to multivariate outputs by a feature-extraction-then-aggregation construction. The counting rule underneath is what binds a mode-share calibration: K shares that sum to one contain K-1 independent numbers, so scoring twelve modelled modes against a five-mode survey does not supply twelve independent targets. The only way to buy identifiability for more parameters is to add targets of a DIFFERENT kind - link counts, boardings, trip-length and duration distributions - not more shares of the same total. The OD-calibration literature reaches the same place from the other side: 'the problem is underdetermined ... there are typically an infinite number of vectors x that can reproduce these counts', which is why a regularisation term toward a prior seed matrix is standard.Nothing by itself, and that is exactly the finding: it is the constraint every other recommendation must pass. Four independent numbers cannot move nine deviations - heavy_rail +247.2%, taxi +178.4%, bike +147.4%, ferry -65.6%, bus +54.6%, light_rail -47.2%, ride -38.0%, motorbike +13.7%, walk -11.1%. The lever is to BUY independent targets of a different kind: CAL.objective.include_counts is false today (enforced at src/calibrate/calibrate.py:391-398), and the disclosed rail and tram boardings that already back the heavy_rail and light_rail targets are scored but are not in the objective either. Each independent target added is one more parameter the loop is allowed to move.

Validation percentages are therefore reported by functional class and against screenlines rather than link by link.Truck sits at 7.35 against 15.47 on a network-wide road-vehicle basis and car at +5.4%; link counts are the observation that would separate "too few car trips" from "car trips on the wrong links". GTFS is the interoperable timetable format because timetables change too often for OSM; the join between the two (pt2matsim here) is the recurring failure point.Supply completeness is ruled out as a cause of the PT deviations: bus +54.6%, light_rail -47.2% and heavy_rail +247.2% all run on a fully mapped schedule. That is a useful elimination for the report.

K1Sample fraction and scaling rulesINRUN.sample.fraction with flowCapacityFactor = fraction (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1280), RUN.sample.storage_capacity_exponent (src/run/run_matsim.py:394-400) and RUN.sample.transit_capacity_scaling / transit_capacity_floor; src/run/sample_population.py:28 records why seats must scale or "crowding silently disappears"Downscaling has measured limits: simulations at 25% or higher of the traveller population preserve all major urban traffic statistics, while below 10% even average statistics become unreliable, with scores and travel times the first to degrade. The scaling rule is that flowCapacityFactor follows the sample share and storageCapacityFactor is set a little higher at samples of 10% or below; in one published scenario a 1% population needed a 2% flow capacity factor to reproduce the observed travel-distance distribution.The whole board is read at 25% under a standing 25%-only directive, and rail and tram are reported as boardings x1/fraction. heavy_rail's +247.2% is therefore a scaled number, and the scaling rule is the thing that has to be right for it to mean anything.
K2Iteration count and costPARTIALRUN.controler.last_iteration is still 1000 at HEAD and was deliberately NOT re-declared to 250 because DECISIONS.md 9.7 measured 250 insufficient. src/analyse/arm_cost.py:182-185 prices an arm from the runs on disk, and was rewritten this week (PR #160) to price on the iteration the arm actually repeats rather than on a blended median. Two new probe overlays were declared for the pace question (cities/newcastle/overlays/runs/f30_plain_probe_25pct.json and f30_evt2_probe_25pct.json), and src/analyse/compare_runs.py is new - a phase-by-phase two-run comparison that refuses a cross-family or cross-fraction comparison as a BLOCKER unless --anyway stamps the reason into the output.There is no standard iteration count: the process is run until the average population score stabilises, simple car-only scenarios converge fast, complex multimodal ones sometimes do not converge by iteration 100, one published scenario converged at iteration 164 and others run 500; because the simulation is stochastic, deterministic convergence criteria do not apply.This is why the board is read at iteration 20 and why "Inside 10%: none" is not yet a finding about the model. GOAL.md requires convergence in at most 250 iterations and that requirement is UNMEASURED. Every ranked mover below is worth less than the arm that would let one be read.
K3Reproducibility of a runPARTIALThe build side is fully deterministic and hashed (B.seed.master = 20260810, MANIFEST.csv over 512 files); the RUN side is not - DECISIONS 3.5 records ~18% of pt2matsim route link sequences differing between identical builds, and src/java/citysim/GradientTableProbe was written precisely because "a run here is not bit-reproducible and a diff could not" prove the table identical (3,266,754 comparisons instead)Run-to-run reproducibility is not achievable by fixing a seed alone in this class of model: across 100 seeds relative errors up to 10% occur on high-volume links, and between-seed variation dominates the last-two-iteration within-seed variation. Reporting a single seeded run is therefore reporting one draw from a distribution.It forbids comparing any two readings from different builds, which is why every family boundary invalidates the arm before it. Combined with the unmeasured seed variance, it means no deviation on the board carries a confidence interval.

The session's directive, answered

Equilibrium: the methods, the architectures, and what to do

Can machine learning or a different architecture reach equilibrium across twelve simultaneous targets? Yes — and the cheapest credible route is not the ML one, which is the finding that matters.

The methods, priced in full simulation runs

One evaluation here costs 7.66 h. Every published method below is quoted at the evaluation count its own source states; where the source does not state one, it says unknown rather than a guess.

MethodFamilyWhat it isEvaluationsPublished applicationApplicability hereOdds
ASC adjustment fixed-point loop (matsim-python-tools `calibration`, Rakow & Nagel)fixed-pointAfter each outer round, shift each mode's alternative-specific constant by the log ratio of target share to modelled share, relative to a fixed reference mode, then re-run the simulation. VERBATIM from `CalibratorBase.calc_asc_update` in matsim-python-tools: `return math.log(z_i) - math.log(m_i) - (math.log(z_0) - math.log(m_0))` where z is the observed share, m the simulated share, and subscript 0 the fixed reference mode (default 'walk'; its ASC stays 0). Damping is a learning-rate schedule: `linear_scheduler(start=0.6, end=1, interval=3)` — the first outer runs are damped to 0.6 of the full step and the step reaches full size by run 3. The module also ships `calib_asc_dist.py` (ASCs by distance class), `calib_group_asc.py` (ASCs by population group) and `constraints.py`, and drives the outer loop through Optuna trials.One full simulation run per outer round. Published applications report a small number of rounds — the TUM thesis brief states Rakow et al. (2025) 'show how automatic ASC calibration using log-difference adjustments can DRAMATICALLY IMPROVE mode-share convergence, replacing legacy manual efforts' for Open Berlin. Agency practice with the identical formula (ActivitySim/ARC/CMAP/WFRC) runs a handful to a few dozen rounds with a dampening factor of 0.5 applied to stop oscillation. Order of magnitude here: 5-15 outer runs.MATSim Open Berlin (Rakow, Kreuschner & Nagel 2025, Transportation Research Procedia 86, 732-739); Rakow & Nagel 2024, 'Automated calibration of alternative specific constants in agent based transport models', TU Berlin DepositOnce. Open Berlin is calibrated on traffic counts, modal split AND mode-specific trip DISTANCE DISTRIBUTIONS — the three together, because the constants alone do not fix the third.DIRECTLY applicable to the modes whose gap is a marginal-utility gap: bike (+147.4%), bus (+54.6%), light_rail (-47.2%), walk (-11.1%), motorbike (+13.7%), car (+5.4%). The deviations across twelve modes sum to +0.086 pp (STATUS.md), i.e. this is a near-closed system — exactly the regime in which a share-simplex fixed point is well behaved, because moving one constant necessarily moves the others' shares and the update accounts for that through the reference term. The repo already has the mathematics in one place: `solve_asc_ride.py:102-120` runs a secant on log(ride/car), which is the same fixed point restricted to one dimension.
blocked by: DECISIONS 8.5 `held_fixed` on all six mode constants, whose rule text requires 'a departure logged in DECISIONS.md BEFORE results are seen'. Also: ferry and motorbike have no constant field to move; the loop's `n_free_allowed`=4 guard would refuse ten; and the loop's grid search would have to be replaced by the log update (a grid over ten constants is combinatorially impossible, a fixed point over ten is one run per round).		medium-high
BLP / Berry contraction-mapping inversion of shares to constantsaggregate-estimationThe industrial-organisation method for recovering mean utilities from AGGREGATE market shares with no unit records. Berry (1994): in the plain-logit case the inversion is closed form, delta_j = log(s_j) - log(s_0). BLP (1995) generalise it to random coefficients through the fixed-point iteration delta_{n+1} = delta_n + log(S) - log(s_hat(delta_n; theta_2)), whose contraction property guarantees convergence. THIS IS ALGEBRAICALLY THE SAME OBJECT AS THE MATSim ASC LOOP: put the MATSim reference mode where BLP put the outside good and the two update rules are identical. That is worth saying plainly, because it means the ASC loop is not a heuristic — it is a contraction with a convergence proof under conditions this model plausibly satisfies (shares strictly positive, utility additively separable in the constant).In BLP the inner loop is cheap because s_hat is a simulated integral, not an agent-based day. Here every contraction step costs one MATSim run, so the count is the number of contraction steps: typically 5-20 to a tolerance of 1e-3 in relative share, fewer with damping.Berry (1994); Berry, Levinsohn & Pakes (1995). The convergence properties of the BLP contraction and faster alternatives are studied directly.It is the theoretical licence for the ASC loop under aggregate-only data, and it names the identification condition precisely: with J alternatives and J-1 independent share observations, the constants are EXACTLY identified and nothing else is. That is the honest boundary of what aggregate mode shares can buy — constants, and only constants. Slopes (value of time, distance sensitivity) are NOT identified by shares alone and must come from unit records or literature.
blocked by: Nothing methodological. The same DECISIONS 8.5 freeze.		high
Cadyts — Bayesian per-plan utility offsets calibrated inside one runfixed-pointFlötteröd's calibration tool, a first-class MATSim contrib and a chapter of the MATSim book (Ch. 32). Rather than an outer loop of full runs, it exploits the randomness already in MATSim's plan choice: the simulation is treated as a complete behavioural PRIOR, and observed counts update it. Each agent's available plans receive a small additive utility offset before they choose, computed from the Bayesian posterior — positive where the observed count exceeds the simulated one, negative where it falls short. The correction happens WITHIN a single simulation run, iteration by iteration, not as an outer loop. A public-transit variant calibrates agent-based PT path choice to count data.ONE simulation run (the offsets converge inside its iterations). This is its decisive advantage over every outer-loop method here.Flötteröd, Bierlaire & Nagel, 'Bayesian demand calibration for dynamic traffic simulations', Transportation Science 45(4):541-561, 2011; behavioural calibration of the large-scale Zurich MATSim microsimulation; 'Automatic calibration of agent-based public transit assignment path choice to count data', TR-C 2016.Tempting and DANGEROUS. It would fit heavy rail and light rail boardings to the Opal series inside one run at essentially zero extra cost. But it is the purest possible form of the thing this project's rules forbid: a per-agent, per-plan utility offset whose only justification is that it makes the counts match. It also cannot be used against traffic counts here at all — `CAL.objective.include_counts` is derived FALSE because the external tier carries no through traffic (DECISIONS 9.14/9.15), and the same argument applies to any boardings series the model is structurally unable to reproduce.
blocked by: The project's own no-compensating-constants rule, and DECISIONS 9.14/9.15 by direct analogy. Would need an explicit, recorded departure and would arguably invalidate the light-rail counterfactual the study exists to answer.		high
Metamodel-assisted simulation-based optimisation (Osorio)surrogate-BOCombine a general-purpose local surrogate (a quadratic polynomial) with a PHYSICAL surrogate — an analytical queueing-network model of the same city — and optimise the combination inside a derivative-free trust region. The physical half supplies global structure the polynomial cannot, so the method works under budgets where a pure surrogate is still random.MEASURED AND SMALL. Osorio & Bierlaire (2013) evaluate at budgets of n = 10, 50, 100 and 150 simulation runs; the metamodel method Am produces an improved signal plan AT n = 10 and dominates the general-purpose quadratic surrogate at every budget, while the pure surrogate is WORSE than the initial plan at n = 10 and only catches up around n = 40. The larger Lausanne subnetwork has 51 decision variables, 102 lanes, 621 endogenous queueing variables.Osorio & Bierlaire, 'A Simulation-Based Optimization Framework for Urban Transportation Problems', Operations Research 61(6):1333-1345, 2013 (Lausanne signal control). History matching / implausibility with an emulator (and ABC)aggregate-estimationDo not optimise. Instead RULE OUT. Fit a cheap emulator to a space-filling design, compute an implausibility score for each candidate parameter vector (distance from the observation, scaled by ALL the uncertainties — observation error, emulator error, and declared model discrepancy), and discard everything above a threshold (conventionally 3, from Pukelsheim's 3-sigma rule). What survives is the NROY set — Not Ruled Out Yet. Repeat in waves, refitting the emulator inside the surviving space.Measured, in a direct ABM study: a 2-parameter birds model used 3 waves of 50 Latin-hypercube design points each with 30 replicate runs, 3,185 total model runs for HM+ABC against 'over 11,000 runs' for ABC alone — HM roughly HALVED the cost. A 16-model-structure farming case used 3 waves and 1,600 runs. 'Every mode inside 10%' is not a least-squares objective — it is an IMPLAUSIBILITY THRESHOLD, and the set of parameter vectors satisfying it is an NROY set. This reframing also dissolves a live problem: it gives a principled place to put MODEL DISCREPANCY, the term that says 'the model has no crowding disutility, so its heavy-rail prediction carries an extra known error'. Declaring discrepancy is the methodologically honest alternative to absorbing it into a constant. What is affordable

The ASC log-ratio fixed point — one simulation run per outer round, five to fifteen rounds. At 7.66 h that is 38–115 hours, i.e. two to five days. It is also mathematically the same object as the BLP contraction (five to twenty steps), which is worth saying because it makes the move a well-understood inversion rather than a fudge.

Osorio's analytical metamodel is the most sample-efficient thing found anywhere: on the OD problem where SPSA moved error 120% → 117% in fifteen iterations, the metamodel went 120% → 32% within one simulation iteration, and it produced an improved plan at n=10 over 51 variables. It needs an analytic queueing companion model this project does not have.

What is not

SPSA in DTA practice: ~700 iterations × ~6 evaluations ≈ thousands of runs — about 8,500 hours here. No.

Cross-entropy: 98,304 evaluations for a three-intersection SUMO model. Categorically out of reach.

Bayesian optimisation with a random-forest surrogate is the strongest ML result in the survey — 477 behavioural parameters of SimMobility MT fitted against aggregate mode shares alone, best point after ~150 evaluations. That is 1,149 h ≈ 48 days here at 25%, or ~21 days at a 10% arm. Finite, unattended, and roughly the length of this project so far — worth holding in reserve, not worth starting with.

The architectures, and why agencies hit mode targets

ArchitectureHow it reaches equilibriumWhy agencies hit their targets with itWhat it would take hereWhat it would break
MATSim co-evolutionary replanning (this project)Each agent keeps a memory of scored plans (here `RUN.replanning.max_agent_plan_memory`=8) and iteratively mutates, executes and re-scores them. The solution concept is an agent-based STOCHASTIC USER EQUILIBRIUM, and the convergence test is that the average population score stabilises — a stochastic criterion, not a deterministic one. Phase oscillations become rarer and vanish in the long run as more stochasticity enters the process.THEY DON'T, directly. They hit them by adjusting mode constants between runs — the ASC loop — which is the same procedure agencies use in their ABMs, just applied to a simulator instead of to a closed-form model. The MATSim book itself records that 'in practical applications, mode-specific constants are adjusted to achieve a better match between the mode share of the simulation output and expected real-world values'.Nothing — it is what is running.N/A. But note the specific pathology this project has and generic MATSim does not: mode availability is GATED. `GatedSubtourModeChoice` 'refuses `ride` on a trip nobody drives', so ride's level is set by how many bound trips the four binder passes in `build_activity_chains.py` created, not by ride's utility. The co-evolutionary loop cannot innovate its way to more ride, whatever the constant says.
Four-step with a mode-split modelFixed-point iteration between a static (Wardrop) assignment and the demand model; the mode split is an algebraic logit at the zone-pair level.Because the mode share is a formula. Calibrating it is solving an equation, not searching. The 'calibration' step is exactly the log(observed/predicted) constant adjustment with a dampening factor.Abandon the microsimulation.GOAL.md requirements 1, 3, 4, 5 — every one of the reasons the project exists.

The calibration adjustments are 'calculated based on the comparison between observed and predicted distributions, computed by taking the natural log of the observed shares divided by the predicted shares', with 'a dampening factor (typically set to 0.5) applied to the constants to help eliminate oscillating patterns between iterations'. Same formula, cheap evaluations, done to convergence. Targets are tour and trip mode shares by purpose, mode and auto sufficiency.Estimating an ActivitySim-style mode choice model requires HTS UNIT RECORDS. Blocked. Its real use here would be as the PHYSICAL surrogate in an Osorio-style metamodel — a tractable analytic companion that carries global structure between the expensive evaluations.Everything, if adopted wholesale; nothing, if used only as a metamodel component.
Reinforcement-learning agentsAgents learn policies by reward; the population converges to an approximate equilibrium of learned policies.They do not — no agency production model uses this. MATSim's own replanning is already a co-evolutionary learning loop over plan memory; swapping in an RL policy changes the learner, not the identification problem.A research programme, a reward function that would itself have to be calibrated, and the same aggregate-only data ceiling.Interpretability, the registry discipline (a learned policy is not a declared value with a sweep), and the ability to attribute a scenario result to a named parameter.

Machine learning: what it buys, and what it cannot

Possible on aggregate data

  • ALTERNATIVE-SPECIFIC CONSTANTS, exactly identified. With J alternatives and J-1 independent share observations the constants are exactly identified and recoverable in closed form in the plain-logit case (Berry 1994: delta_j = log s_j - log s_0) or by the BLP contraction otherwise. This is the whole of what aggregate shares buy, and it is enough for the 10% bar.
  • ASCs by SEGMENT where segment-level shares are published — the matsim-python-tools module ships `calib_group_asc.py` for exactly this, and agency practice targets tour mode share by purpose and auto sufficiency.
  • ASCs by DISTANCE CLASS where a distance distribution is published — `calib_asc_dist.py`. Open Berlin calibrates 'traffic counts, modal split AND mode-specific trip distance distributions' together, which is the published answer to the trip-length half of this project's problem.
  • Bayesian calibration against aggregate summary statistics: GP emulator + posterior, or history matching with an implausibility threshold and an NROY set. Both accept aggregate moments and both make MODEL DISCREPANCY an explicit, declared term rather than something a constant silently absorbs.
  • Method of simulated moments / indirect inference against aggregate moments — the general form of the above; identification is limited to as many parameters as there are independent moments, which is the same count as the ASC result.
  • Cadyts-style Bayesian correction against counts and boardings, which uses only aggregate observations — technically available, methodologically disallowed here (see the tension).

Blocked without unit records

  • Any ESTIMATED discrete choice model — MNL, nested logit, mixed logit. The C1 nested-logit specification with nesting coefficients 0.65/0.8/0.7 is currently `assumed`/`placeholder`, and it cannot become `estimated` without unit records.
  • Every ML behaviour model in the survey. The Deep Activity Model needs ~197k individual activity records to pretrain and ~8k-100k to transfer; its authors state that 'aggregate statistics alone cannot capture the interdependencies among household members and sequential activity patterns necessary for model training'. Gradient-boosted and neural mode-choice classifiers all train on person-level choice sets, and the ML advantage over MNL is explicitly reported to grow with data volume and to vanish when data is scarce.
  • Inverse reinforcement learning on observed activity sequences — same requirement, person-level trajectories.
  • SLOPE parameters from shares. Value of time, distance sensitivity and the time weights are NOT identified by aggregate shares; they must stay literature-sourced (which they are: C.vot.*, C.time_weights.* are `literature`) or come from unit records.
  • The transfer penalty. `C1_parameters.json` records the estimation route as 'NOT ESTIMABLE FROM THIS PACKAGE - see DECISIONS.md 9.32': the proposal asks for tap-on/tap-off TIMING and every Opal source held is a monthly aggregate.

The honest ML verdict

Learned behaviour models are cleanly blocked. The Deep Activity Model line needs roughly 197,000 individual records and its authors state explicitly that aggregate statistics cannot substitute; the NSW HTS is aggregate-only and the TfNSW unit-record request is outstanding. Worse, the benchmark literature carries a sting for this specific project: neural choice models reach 89.03% trip-level accuracy against multinomial logit on 14,671 NHTS trips, yet the most accurate learners are the worst at reproducing aggregate mode share — which is the only statistic this project's board scores. LLM-agent mobility simulators are further off still: trip-duration error of 24.4 minutes against a 0.29-minute reference variability.

Machine learning's real contribution here is not a behaviour model. It is a surrogate over the simulator — an emulator that predicts the twelve-mode scoreboard from a parameter vector, so that most candidates are scored in milliseconds and only the informative ones are actually run. That is the Tallinn result, and it is the one ML route this project's data constraint does not block.

The objective function is the cheapest thing to fix, and nothing works without it

current

`CAL.objective.components` = {`mode_share.mean_abs_pp`: 1.0} — the unweighted MEAN of ABSOLUTE deviations, in PERCENTAGE POINTS, over the FIVE foldable HTS categories (car+motorbike folded together, bike+taxi folded together, PT folded across bus/tram/rail/ferry). C5 records best_objective 10.65. Constraints (occupancy, trip length) are feasibility filters, not terms.

goal implies

A MINIMAX / CONSTRAINT-SATISFACTION objective over TWELVE UNFOLDED modes in RELATIVE per cent: minimise max_m |dev_m| subject to max_m |dev_m| <= 10%, with a hard stop at 20%. These are different problems and they disagree in the direction that matters. A mean over folded categories can improve while the goal gets worse: car +5.4% and motorbike +13.7% fold to a car+motorbike error near zero, so the current objective is BLIND to the mode that is second-nearest to failing. Likewise bike +147.4% and taxi +178.4% fold against a single 'Other' target. The objective the loop optimises cannot see seven of the twelve modes as separate quantities at all.

literature

The right formal frame for 'every target inside a tolerance' is NOT least squares — it is HISTORY MATCHING. An implausibility statistic scales each target's deviation by all its uncertainties (observation, emulator, and declared model discrepancy) and rejects any parameter vector whose implausibility exceeds a threshold, conventionally 3 by Pukelsheim's 3-sigma rule; what survives is the NROY set, 'the set of parameter combinations judged non-implausible'. Note that this is a MAX over targets, i.e. minimax, and that it is a SET-VALUED answer rather than a point — which is the correct answer to a satisficing goal. Agency practice arrives at the same place informally: the WFRC model reports 'all mode shares were calibrated to within 5% of observed data' as a per-mode tolerance, not as an aggregate statistic. This project's own C5 constraint machinery (`feasible`/`violations`) is already the right shape and is simply not connected to the search.

source url

https://www.jasss.org/25/2/1.html ; https://wfrc.utah.gov/wftdm-docs/v9x/v920/validation/3-modechoice.html

recommendation

Replace `mode_share.mean_abs_pp` with a twelve-mode implausibility-style objective: primary term max_m |dev_m| / tol_m over the twelve modes on their OWN bases (relative per cent for share modes, boardings for rail and tram), with tol_m = 10; tie-break on the count of modes outside 10%; and carry each mode's declared target sweep in the denominator so that a mode whose target is an interval (taxi 0.744-1.240, ferry 0.000-0.286) is not scored as if its target were a point. Add a DECLARED MODEL DISCREPANCY per mode — heavy rail's missing crowding disutility is a known, nameable discrepancy — so the objective can distinguish 'the parameters are wrong' from 'the model is missing a mechanism'. This is a change to `cities/newcastle/registry/CAL_calibration.json` plus `src/calibrate/fit.py`, costs zero machine hours, and is testable against the existing `_fit.json` files on disk.

Why Phase 2 is the decisive experiment

Unfreeze three constants, create the two that do not exist, keep rail, ride and walk frozen with a stated per-mode reason, and run two damped fixed-point rounds. The observable is not the mode shares. It is whether |Δasc| shrinks between round 1 and round 2. Contraction means the residual really is taste and constants will close it; no contraction means the residual is mechanism and no constant ever will. Either answer ends a question this project has been circling for eleven families, for about fifteen machine hours.

And it is comparable with itself: a C.asc.* change is a run-inputs rebuild off the already-mapped schedule, so DECISIONS.md §3.5 is not engaged and round 2 legitimately compares with round 1 — which almost nothing in this project's 31-boundary history has been able to claim.

Would the process survive an automated search?

RuleFileBlocks a search?Essential?Why
One arm at a timecities/newcastle/docs/GOAL.md:94; cities/newcastle/docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:62; cities/newcastle/docs/NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:98; cities/newcastle/docs/STATUS.md:194; issue #66blocksconventionThis is a machine-capacity rule with a measured basis, not a validity rule. The evidence in positions/runs-and-economics.md:62 is: three arms declared 78 GiB on a 63.5 GiB machine and the pagefile grew 8.1 -> 19.1 GiB (9.5), and the #66 stall hit both concurrent arms at the same wall-clock time. The same line states the distinction an outer loop needs exactly: 'Iteration count survives contention; iteration duration does not.' So a MODE READING taken under contention is citable and a WALL-CLOCK measurement is not. An automated search evaluates mode readings, so it can run arms in parallel on hardware that fits them - and must not price an arm from a contended run. Concretely: the memory model at positions/runs-and-economics.md:54 (~24 GiB fixed + 0.09-0.3 MB/agent, 33-38 GiB working set at 25 %) says this 63.5 GiB workstation fits exactly one 25 % arm, so on THIS machine the rule is arithmetic, not policy. Relaxing it means buying memory, not changing a document. An outer loop on this host is inherently serial and its throughput ceiling is ~1.1 arms/day at 21.8 h each - which is the single hardest fact about automating calibration here.
The comparability family - one build of the network per comparison; nothing run before a boundary compares with anything after itcities/newcastle/docs/DECISIONS.md 3.5; cities/newcastle/docs/run_families.json (31 families in 23 days); .claude/CLAUDE.md (Hard constraints); enforced in code by src/analyse/compare_runs.pydoes not blockessentialTHIS IS THE RULE THAT MOST PEOPLE WOULD EXPECT TO BLOCK A SEARCH AND IT DOES NOT - it DEFINES the legal search space, which is more useful. The rule exists because pt2matsim's schedule mapping is not reproducible (~18 % of route link sequences differ between identical builds) and because any change to the demand, the network or the Java changes what a run means. A parameter search that varies only REGISTRY SCALARS in the behaviour and scoring layers (the C.* fields, the mode constants, the marginal utilities) opens NO family: cities/newcastle/docs/run_families.json shows all 31 boundaries were opened by demand rebuilds, network patches, binder changes and Java edits - never by a scored parameter value. So the family rule says, precisely: an outer loop over C-layer scalars on a frozen network and a frozen plans set is legitimate and every arm in it is mutually comparable; an outer loop that touches the binder, the router, the demand or the Java is not a search but a sequence of incomparable single points. That is exactly the boundary an automated calibrator needs drawn, and it is already drawn, already dated, and already machine-checked - src/analyse/compare_runs.py REFUSES a comparison across a family, a fraction or a profiled/unprofiled pair unless --anyway stamps the reason into the output (docs/README.md:34-36). An outer loop inherits that refusal for free. KEEP IT UNCHANGED. Two corollaries the loop must obey: (a) the family must be opened ONCE, before the sweep, and not touched during it; (b) because a family boundary invalidates every prior arm, a search interrupted by a code fix has to restart, so the loop must be able to run to completion inside one boundary.
MATSim runs are not bit-reproducible; any A/B claim needs a multi-run band, never a diffcities/newcastle/docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:55 (three runs of ONE unmodified build on the same package and the same seed gave 5,620,710 / 5,620,410 / 5,620,710 iteration-0 events, and every pair diverges by iteration 2; MatsimRandom.getLocalInstance() increments an unsynchronised static counter under global.numberOfThreads = 20)does not blockessentialNot a process convention at all - a property of the instrument, and the hardest constraint on the OBJECTIVE FUNCTION of any automated search. A single arm per parameter point is a noisy sample, and the noise floor has been measured only for mode shares ('Mode shares were identical across all three, so a gate reading is not at risk'). That is reassuring for a gate reading at 3 significant figures and NOT sufficient for an optimiser that will chase differences smaller than the seed spread. Any outer loop must either (a) replicate each point across seeds and optimise the band, at N x 21.8 h per point, or (b) declare a minimum detectable effect below which it refuses to prefer one point over another. This single fact, more than any document rule, is what makes gradient-free search over this simulator expensive.
No launch while an open issue lacks awaiting-runcities/newcastle/docs/GOAL.md:56-61; src/run/issue_gate.py; run.py refuses before a launch; README.md:92-93blocksconventionA pure process convention, and the one that would stop an automated loop dead - not because it is hard to satisfy but because it consults an EXTERNAL, HUMAN-EDITED tracker in the middle of a machine loop. Anyone opening an issue mid-sweep halts the sweep at an arbitrary point, which for a search is worse than never starting: an interrupted sweep inside a family cannot simply resume if the interruption was a code fix. It should be relaxed for a search that never claims a result, and the relaxation is principled rather than convenient: requirement 10's purpose (GOAL.md:56) is 'before the simulator is TUNED OR TESTED', i.e. before a run whose reading will be believed. A sweep arm that produces a point in a parameter surface and is explicitly not citable as a result is outside the rule's purpose. Concretely: give the launcher a `--sweep <sweep-id>` mode that (a) writes `citable: false` and the sweep id into `_run.json`, (b) bypasses issue_gate.py, (c) makes report_mode_ridership.py and fit.py refuse to quote the run as a standalone reading, and (d) requires the sweep's WINNER to be re-run as a normal, issue-gated, approved arm before anything is claimed from it. The gate then applies exactly where results are made.
A stated-cost approval from the user, spent on use; no approval is ever standingREADME.md:89; cities/newcastle/docs/NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:95-96; cities/newcastle/docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:61; cities/newcastle/docs/STATUS.md:193blocksconventionPer-arm human approval is incompatible with any loop by definition - a 20-point sweep is 20 approvals over 18 days at 21.8 h an arm. But the rule protects something real: positions/runs-and-economics.md:33-34 records an arm quoted at ~22 h that ran at 31 h and had to be stopped, and 34 states the lesson as 'a stated cost is a boundary, not an estimate'. The right relaxation is to move the boundary up a level: ONE stated-cost approval for the whole sweep, expressed as a machine-hour budget and a point count, with the loop refusing to launch the next arm once the budget is spent and writing the remaining budget into every `_run.json`. That preserves the property the rule exists for (an operator knows and bounds what is being spent) while removing the per-arm handshake. Note this rule is currently enforced by NOTHING (README.md:87 says the launcher enforces the issue gate, not this one), so automating it would make it stronger than it is today, not weaker.
25 % runs onlycities/newcastle/docs/NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:97 (user directive, 1 September 2026); README.md:90blocksconventionThis is the rule I would relax FIRST for a search, and it is currently unenforced anyway (cities/newcastle/registry/RUN_execution.json declares RUN.sample.fraction with sweep [0.01, 0.4], so a 10 % run passes every check). A coarse-to-fine search - screen at 10 % to rank the parameter space, confirm the top few at 25 % - is the standard way to make an expensive simulator searchable, and the project has the evidence to price it: positions/runs-and-economics.md:51 records the 10 % economics at 170.9-182.1 s/it solo and ~18-21 h per 300, i.e. a 10 % arm to the iteration-100 gate is roughly 5 h against 6.1 h at 25 %, so the saving is smaller than it looks and the case is weaker than it appears. The real objection to relaxing it is 9.10 and 9.12, which measured 1 % unusable and found the answer SPLITS by fraction - so a 10 % ranking is only useful if the ranking is shown to be fraction-invariant, which nobody has measured. That measurement (do the top-k parameter points at 10 % agree with the top-k at 25 %?) is itself a cheap and high-value probe. Either way, if the directive is to stand it belongs in the registry as a held_fixed rule, not only in prose.
No result before a run's _run.json says ran_to_last_iteration; a stopped arm is citable at its reached_iteration and nowhere past itcities/newcastle/docs/GOAL.md:89-93; cities/newcastle/docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:9 and :17; enforced in src/calibrate and the output schemasdoes not blockessentialMUST SURVIVE UNCHANGED, and it is the rule that determines what an outer loop is even allowed to optimise. Every arm since F4 has stopped at its iteration-100 gate, so every point an outer loop could evaluate today is a NON-CONVERGED reading. Optimising a parameter surface evaluated at iteration 100 of a 1000-iteration relaxation is optimising a transient, and the project's own record says so: 9.7 measured 250 iterations insufficient, and RUN.controler.last_iteration stays 1000 (STATUS.md:44). An automated search built on gate readings would tune the model's approach path rather than its equilibrium. This is the deepest obstacle to automated calibration here and it is not a document problem at all - it is that the inner loop has never been observed to converge. Any credible outer loop needs first to establish that the iteration-100 ranking of parameter points predicts the iteration-1000 ranking; if it does not, the loop is optimising noise no matter how it is implemented.
/handoff discipline - one session, one record section (<=140 lines) with an index row and a section-14 row, position pages rewritten, the board regenerated, ONE pull request watched to merge.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md (Phases 1-7); .claude/CLAUDE.md (Conventions); cities/newcastle/tests/doc_shape.json (record.max_new_section_lines 140, brief.max_lines 180, board.max_hand_lines 170)does not blockconventionIt does not block a search - a sweep is one session - but its shape assumes a session produces one narrative. A 20-arm sweep produces 20 evidence rows and one conclusion, and forcing that into a 140-line prose section would either truncate the evidence or blow the cap (which, via .claude/hooks/gate-pr-on-docs.sh, would then block the PR). The relaxation that keeps the value: let a sweep write ONE record section that states the sweep's design, its family, its budget, its objective and its winner, and have the per-arm evidence live as a GENERATED artefact (a sweep table under results/processed/ plus a generated block on the position page), regenerated like the board's blocks rather than written by hand. That is consistent with the repository's own strongest pattern - generated blocks between markers, checked by --check - and it removes the temptation the board already shows: STATUS.md:150 hand-writes a count the generator carries, which is how '161 runs' survived beside '162 run directories'. The parts that must not be relaxed: every figure carries its source, a correction lands on the position page plus a section-14 row and never as a rewrite of dated text, and the record stays append-only.
The calibration objective itself - what an automated loop would be optimisingcities/newcastle/params/C5_calibration.json; src/calibrate/fit.py:79-84; cities/newcastle/data/processed/validation/mode_targets_by_mode.csvdoes not blockessentialNOT A PROCESS RULE, but the finding most relevant to the directive and it emerged from reading the document layer, so it belongs here. THE GOAL'S SCOREBOARD AND THE CALIBRATION OBJECTIVE ARE TWO DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT SYSTEMS. The twelve-mode scoreboard the board and GOAL requirement 7 are stated on comes from data/processed/validation/mode_targets_by_mode.csv - 12 rows, each on its own basis (share of resident linked trips for eight, boardings per weekday for two, level-only for truck, representation for freight rail), and that file has NO `split` column, so it is outside the 67/143 pre-registration entirely. The calibration objective that src/calibrate/calibrate.py would optimise is C5_calibration.json's `objective_components: {mode_share.mean_abs_pp: 1.0}`, computed by fit.py over FIVE FOLDED HTS categories (Vehicle driver = car+motorbike, Vehicle passenger = ride, Walk only, Public transport = all four PT modes folded, Other = bike) carrying, by the calibration report's own statement, FOUR independent degrees of freedom. An automated outer loop wired to the existing calibrator would therefore optimise four folded numbers while the goal is stated on twelve unfolded ones - and the folding is exactly where the goal's hardest modes disappear: heavy rail (+247.2 %) and light rail (-47.2 %) are opposite-signed and both inside the single 'Public transport' cell, so a parameter change that made both worse in opposite directions could improve the objective. Before ANY architecture question (ML, surrogate, Bayesian optimisation) is worth asking, the objective has to be re-expressed over the twelve targets the goal is stated on. C5_calibration.json also already records `search_declined` with its reason - 'the loop can legitimately move only these parameters, at ~21 full 25 % x 1000 runs; neither reaches the structural misfits (9.25, 9.28)' and `free_parameters: []` - which is the project's own dated judgement that the outer loop as built cannot reach the problem. That judgement is about the PARAMETER SET, and it is worth revisiting now that the behaviour layer has grown to 53 C.* fields; the judgement about the OBJECTIVE has not been made and is the prior question.

The comparability rule does not block a parameter search — it defines one

All 31 family boundaries came from demand, network or Java changes; not one came from moving a scored scalar. So a C-layer sweep on a frozen build is legal under the project's own rule, and compare_runs.py already enforces the boundary. What actually blocks a search are three conventions — the issue gate, per-arm cost approval, and 25%-only — all of which could be relaxed behind a --sweep mode whose runs are explicitly non-citable, with a stated budget. Two things must not be relaxed: MATSim is not bit-reproducible here, so a search must optimise a band and not a point; and ran_to_last_iteration stays the result gate.

Verification sample

Phase 8 requires ten cited locations to be re-read and five freshly searched sources re-fetched. Re-read by hand this pass, all confirmed: STATUS.md:79 (the "is RUNNING" contradiction), STATUS.md:150 against the generated :116 (161 vs 162), README.md:80 (22–31 h vs 18.2–21.8 h), cities/newcastle/params/C5_calibration.json (free_parameters empty, search declined, feasible false, generated 24 August), mode_targets_by_mode.csv (twelve rows on the board's basis), calibrate.py --plan (the five movable fields, quoted verbatim), calibrate.py:111-146 (classification by consumer basename), calibrate.py:486-491 (registry keys down the raw --set path), C_behaviour.json (six constants held_fixed under §8.5), and performance.json's run table (the two 67-hour F4 arms carrying no completion). Reused library rows were verified by inspection — each carries a source URL and a last_verified date inside its horizon — and were deliberately not re-fetched.

Dead research routes, recorded so no later pass pays for them

web.archive.org is blocked by this repository's own network sandbox; MDPI article HTML 403s; ScienceDirect 403s; ResearchGate 403s the agent; arxiv.org/pdf/2112.12071 exceeds the 10 MB fetch limit; CMAP's PDF is an image-only scan; matsim-org/matsim-python-tools 404s (it is under matsim-vsp); the eqasim docs path 404s; the Open Berlin paper 403s and opdyts' page 404s, so their evaluation counts are marked unknown rather than guessed. Two routes that work and should be reused: the Semantic Scholar graph API (three recoveries this pass) and saving a binary PDF fetch locally to read with page ranges, at no search cost.

What this report is not

It is an assessment, not a change. It launched no run, recompiled nothing, opened no issue, and edited no model, data or living document. Nothing in it is a result: only a run whose _run.json says ran_to_last_iteration is one, and none of the readings quoted here comes from such a run.

A reading of commit 6cf0ffd on main, 8 September 2026. Produced by /project-report. Every number is drawn from an artefact, every code finding cites file and line, every research claim cites the source it was read from. Nothing here is a result.
